linkedin:4479200282.desc: About the opportunity Join Cranfield University’s Systems Realization Group (SRG) for an MSc by Research exploring Evolving Cyber-Physical-Social Systems (eCPSS) . This project combines software engineering, data science and human-centred AI to integrate existing research demonstrators into a usable, client-facing decision-support platform. SRG develops and evaluates principles and mechanisms that help engineered systems adapt to changing requirements while preserving safety, accountable human authority and sustainability. Your research will support the translation of these advances into tools that organisations can evaluate and use. Success will involve delivering a working minimum viable product (MVP), documenting its architecture and evaluating how effectively it supports users in completing tasks, understanding recommendations and tracing decisions. Responsibilities Assess existing research demonstrators and identify their integration requirements. Develop a modular software architecture and shared data interfaces. Connect components through APIs or adapters. Build a web interface that enables users to explore operational changes, compare responses and review decision rationale. Retain appropriate human approval and record decisions throughout the workflow. Evaluate integration reliability, usability, task completion and decision traceability using agreed manufacturing scenarios. Collaborate with SRG researchers and demonstrator developers. Produce technical documentation, reproducible installation guidance and an MSc by Research thesis. Qualifications A first- or second-class UK honours degree, or equivalent, in Computer Science or Data Science. Related computing disciplines with equivalent practical experience may also be considered. Strong programming skills in Python or an equivalent language, with evidence of building working software. Ability to work with APIs, structured data, databases and version control. Experience developing user-facing applications. Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work independently and collaboratively. An interest in human-centred design, accountable AI and applied research. Experience with JavaScript/TypeScript, web frameworks, automated testing, AI/LLM integration, knowledge graphs or software deployment is desirable. Prior manufacturing or healthcare experience is not required. Applicants are encouraged to share relevant projects or a portfolio/repository link. Study arrangements This is a self-funded MSc by Research opportunity , rather than a salaried position. The duration is one year full-time or two years part-time , and applications are welcome from UK and international candidates. For enquiries, contact Dr Jelena Milisavljevic Syed at jelenams@cranfield.ac.uk. View the opportunity and apply

linkedin:4478784099.title: Doktorand i atmosfärsvetenskap och oceanografi, med fokus på ML-metoder i klimatmodellering
linkedin:4478784099.desc: Meteorologiska institutionen vid Stockholms universitet (MISU) bedriver forskning och utbildning som rör atmosfären, oceanen, och fysikaliskt-baserad klimatvetenskap. MISU erbjuder utbildningsprogram på kandidat-, master- och forskarnivå. Vår forskning söker svar på grundläggande frågor om atmosfärens och havens dynamiska, fysiska, kemiska, och biogeokemiska egenskaper av relevans för väder och klimat. Vi strävar efter en bred forskningsverksamhet inom vårt vetenskapliga område. Vi studerar frågor som sträcker sig från djuphavet till den övre atmosfären och från tropikerna till polerna. I vår forskning utnyttjar och utvecklar vi teori, statistiska metoder och numeriska modeller i nära samspel med observationer. Dessutom utvecklar och leder institutionen observationsbaserad forskning med stöd av satelliter, arktiska isbrytarexpeditioner och landbaserade instrument. MISU har cirka 60 anställda och ingår i en större forskningsmiljö som inkluderar Bolincentret för klimatforskning, Östersjöcentrum och Swedish e-Science Research Centre. Institutionen har stark internationell prägel, över hälften av medarbetarna har en bakgrund utanför Sverige och både svenska och engelska används som arbetsspråk. Vi välkomnar och värdesätter mångfald i vår arbetsmiljö. Mer information om oss finns på: Meteorologiska institutionen. Projektbeskrivning Moln och deras förändringar till följd av variationer i omgivande miljö spelar en avgörande för klimat och klimatförändringar. Upplösningen i typiska klimatmodeller är dock alldeles för grov för att de ska kunna representera processer relaterade till molnbildning explicit. Dessa processer behöver därför parametriseras, eller representeras som funktioner av storskaliga tillståndsvariabler. Sådana parametriseringar är behäftade med stor osäkerhet, och dessutom är de beräkningsmässigt kostsamma. Det här projektets fokus är att på nya sätt brygga över mellan mikroskala och global skala, för att förbättra klimatmodellers noggrannhet, effektivitet och generaliserbarhet och samtidigt utnyttja modern beräkningshårdvara. Vi kommer att undersöka hur maskininlärningsmodeller (ML-modeller) kan tränas på observationer och resultat från högupplöst modellering, som alternativ till empiriska parmetriseringar av småskaliga processer relaterade till turbulens, molnbildning och aerosol-moln-interaktioner. Specifikt ingår i uppgifterna att utveckla och träna datadrivna modeller, koppla dem till en storskalig klimatmodell, utvärdera resultaten mot mätningar och traditionellt parametriserade modeller, och att använda den ML-förstärkta modellen till att uppskatta klimatrelevans som molns effekt på strålningsbalansen, och strålningsdrivning från aerosol-moln-interaktioner. Arbetet kommer att utföras i nära samarbete med experter inom datavetenskap, inom Swedish e-Science Research Centre, och bidra till metodutveckling med bredare tillämpning än endast klimatvetenskap. Som doktorand i projektet kommer du att utveckla dina färdigheter inom atmosfärsvetenskap och klimatmodellering, men även inom datavetenskap och maskininlärning, samt kommunikation och samarbete inom och mellan discipliner. Behörighetskrav För att bli antagen till forskarutbildning krävs att den sökande har grundläggande och särskild behörighet. Behörigheten ska vara uppfylld senast vid antagning till programmet. Grundläggande behörighet har du, om du avlagt examen på avancerad nivå, eller fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng (hp), varav minst 60 hp på avancerad nivå, eller på annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. För särskild behörighet krävs minst 90 hp i något av ämnena meteorologi, oceanografi, fysik eller kemi, minst 15 hp i matematik och ett självständigt arbete om minst 15 hp. Av detta skall minst 60 hp vara på avancerad nivå. Vidare krävs språkkunskaper i engelska motsvarande engelska B på gymnasiet. Allmän studieplan för utbildning på forskarnivå i atmosfärsvetenskap och oceanografi. Urval Urval bland de sökande som uppfyller behörighetskraven ska göras med hänsyn till deras förmåga att tillgodogöra sig utbildningen. Enbart det förhållandet att en sökande bedöms kunna få tidigare utbildning eller yrkesverksamhet tillgodoräknad för utbildningen får inte vid urval ge sökanden företräde framför andra sökande. Beslut om antagning fattas enligt gällande delegationsordning. Vid bedömningen tas hänsyn till förtrogenhet och skicklighet inom ämnet, förmåga att uttrycka sig i tal och skrift på engelska, analytisk förmåga, kreativitet, initiativförmåga och självständighet, och samarbetsförmåga. Till grund för bedömningen ligger tidigare studiers relevans, betyg på genomgångna högskolekurser (särskilt de på avancerad nivå), kvalitet och omfattning på det självständiga arbetet, referenser, intervjuer samt skriftlig avsiktsförklaring. Antagningsordning för utbildning på forskarnivå vid Stockholms universitet. Om anställningen Tillträde enligt överenskommelse. Vi erbjuder en tidsbegränsad anställning som doktorand enligt 5 kap. högskoleförordningen (1993:100). Anställningstiden får inte vara längre än vad som motsvarar utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid under fyra år. Som doktorand ska du främst ägna dig åt din egen utbildning på forskarnivå, men i anställningen kan arbete med utbildning, forskning och administration ingå i begränsad omfattning (högst 20 %). En ny anställning som doktorand gäller för högst ett år, anställningen förnyas därefter med högst två år i taget. Stockholms universitet värnar om att vara en arbetsplats som är fri från diskriminering och ger lika rättigheter och möjligheter för alla. Kontakt För mer information om projektet, kontakta professor Frida Bender, frida.bender@misu.su.se. För information om forskarutbildningen, kontakta studierektor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se. Upplysningar om rekryteringsprocessen och anställningsvillkor lämnas av administrativ chef, Sara Engström sara.engstrom@misu.su.se. Ansökan Du söker doktorandplatsen via Stockholms universitets rekryteringssystem. Bifoga personligt brev och CV samt de bilagor som efterfrågas i ansökningsformuläret. Du som sökande ansvarar för att ansökan är komplett i enlighet med annonsen och att den är universitetet tillhanda senast sista ansökningsdag. Vi ber att du som sökande avstår från att skicka in en AI-genererad ansökan. Anvisningar för sökande finns på webbsidan: att söka en anställning. Stockholms universitet bidrar till det hållbara demokratiska samhällets utveckling genom kunskap, upplysning och sanningssökande.

linkedin:4479291257.title: Offre de thèse CIFRE Janvier/Février 2027
linkedin:4479291257.desc: Pérennisation soutenable des systèmes de production : modélisation probabiliste hybride et anticipation des risques d’obsolescence Contexte et problématique Une part importante de l’outil industriel repose aujourd’hui sur des installations exploitées depuis plusieurs décennies. Ces moyens de production associent des équipements, composants, automatismes et logiciels dont la durée d’exploitation dépasse fréquemment celle de commercialisation ou de support. L’obsolescence constitue ainsi un risque important pour la continuité de production. Elle peut résulter d’évolutions technologiques, de l’arrêt d’une référence, de la raréfaction de pièces, de la disparition d’un fournisseur, de la fin d’un support ou de la perte de compétences. Sa maîtrise constitue un enjeu de disponibilité des installations, de souveraineté industrielle et d’utilisation raisonnée des ressources. Une installation industrielle comporte plusieurs milliers de références reliées entre elles au sein d’architectures techniques et de chaînes d’approvisionnement complexes. Les informations nécessaires à l’évaluation de leur pérennité sont dispersées entre bases de maintenance, référentiels techniques, données fournisseurs, historiques d’intervention et connaissances métier. Ces informations sont hétérogènes, évolutives et souvent incomplètes. Le module de diagnostic du logiciel OBSOLIO, développé par GreenTrack Genius, évalue actuellement l’obsolescence au moyen d’un scoring expert statique. La thèse vise à dépasser cette approche pour construire un modèle capable d’actualiser et d’anticiper le risque d’obsolescence à partir des données disponibles et des connaissances métier, tout en représentant explicitement l’incertitude et les mécanismes de propagation du risque. Question scientifique centrale Comment modéliser, propager et actualiser le risque d’obsolescence au sein d’une architecture industrielle multiniveau et de sa chaîne d’approvisionnement, en présence d’informations hétérogènes et incomplètes, afin de comparer de manière explicable des stratégies de pérennisation soutenable ? Verrou scientifique et approche proposée Le principal verrou scientifique concerne la propagation probabiliste d’un risque d’obsolescence dans une architecture industrielle multiniveau, depuis le composant jusqu’à l’équipement et à la ligne de production, alors que l’état de connaissance sur les différents éléments du système est incomplet et variable. Une absence d’information sur une référence, un fournisseur ou une possibilité de substitution ne peut en effet être assimilée à l’absence de risque, ni être systématiquement considérée comme une situation défavorable. La modélisation devra donc distinguer autant que possible le risque déduit des informations disponibles de l’incertitude liée à l’incomplétude de ces informations. La recherche s’appuiera sur une approche hybride associant deux niveaux de représentation. 1. Représentation des connaissances et de l’architecture industrielle Un graphe de connaissances sera utilisé pour structurer les relations entre actifs, composants, nomenclatures, fournisseurs, références de substitution, historiques et événements d’obsolescence. Ce graphe aura pour fonction de représenter la structure du système étudié et les informations disponibles. Une question de recherche portera sur la manière de transformer ou d’exploiter cette représentation pour construire les dépendances pertinentes du modèle probabiliste. 2. Modélisation et propagation probabilistes Les réseaux bayésiens constitueront le cadre principal étudié pour agréger les connaissances expertes et les observations disponibles, représenter les dépendances entre facteurs et propager l’incertitude entre les différents niveaux du système. La dimension temporelle sera introduite lorsque les données disponibles permettent de caractériser l’évolution des variables et du risque. Les extensions dynamiques des réseaux bayésiens seront notamment étudiées pour représenter cette évolution et évaluer leur capacité à anticiper une situation d’obsolescence. Le travail portera en particulier sur les méthodes d’initialisation du modèle, l’intégration de connaissances expertes, l’apprentissage à partir des historiques et la robustesse de l’inférence en présence de données manquantes. Aide à la décision et pérennisation soutenable L’objectif est de dépasser le diagnostic pour comparer des stratégies de remédiation. Les réseaux bayésiens pourront être étendus sous forme de diagrammes d’influence, intégrant variables de décision et critères d’utilité. Plusieurs stratégies seront considérées : maintien en l’état, constitution ou mutualisation de stocks, substitution, reconditionnement, reconception partielle ou renouvellement. La pérennisation soutenable sera abordée comme un problème de décision multicritère prenant en compte au minimum : la disponibilité et le risque technique ; le coût de la stratégie ; son impact environnemental ; sa faisabilité industrielle et organisationnelle. L’objectif sera donc d’identifier la solution réduisant le risque d’obsolescence mais aussi de comparer les conséquences de différentes stratégies dans le contexte propre au système étudié. Validation et résultats attendus La validation reposera sur des données industrielles historiques : données de maintenance et d’équipements, informations fournisseurs, changements de références, événements d’obsolescence et autres données de cycle de vie disponibles sur les sites étudiés. Une validation rétrospective sera privilégiée. Elle consistera, lorsque les données le permettent, à reconstruire l’état d’information disponible à une date passée, à produire l’évaluation du risque correspondant, puis à comparer cette évaluation aux événements observés ultérieurement. Les résultats seront également comparés au scoring expert actuellement utilisé dans OBSOLIO afin de mesurer l’apport de la modélisation probabiliste en matière d’anticipation, de gestion des données manquantes et d’explicabilité. La thèse devra aboutir à trois résultats principaux : un modèle formel de représentation et de propagation probabiliste du risque d’obsolescence dans une architecture industrielle multiniveau ; une méthode d’aide à la décision permettant de comparer des stratégies de pérennisation selon plusieurs critères ; un démonstrateur Python mettant en œuvre les modèles développés et permettant leur validation sur des cas industriels. Les contributions scientifiques porteront ainsi sur la représentation et la propagation d’un risque d’obsolescence dans des systèmes industriels complexes lorsque l’information disponible est distribuée, évolutive et incomplète. Les résultats auront vocation à alimenter le moteur algorithmique d’OBSOLIO, sans que le développement du logiciel constitue l’objet de la thèse. Profil recherché Le ou la candidate devra être titulaire d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un master en génie industriel, ingénierie des systèmes, science des données, informatique industrielle ou domaine proche. De solides bases en probabilités, statistiques et modélisation sont attendues, ainsi qu’une bonne maîtrise de la programmation scientifique en Python. Une connaissance des réseaux bayésiens, des modèles graphiques probabilistes ou des méthodes de recherche opérationnelle constituera un atout. Le travail nécessitera également une capacité à comprendre des architectures industrielles complexes et à travailler avec les équipes de maintenance, méthodes, achats et ingénierie. Le profil recherché doit ainsi associer compétences en modélisation et intérêt pour les problématiques industrielles concrètes. Contact : Marc.Zolghadri@isae-supmeca.fr

linkedin:4478427322.desc: Job description: Ph.D. Cadidate (m/f/d) at the Institute for Medical Informatics and Biometry The position is to be filled as soon as possible on a full-time or part-time basis for a fixed term of 36 months. Remuneration is based on the classification provisions of the Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the Federal States (TV-L); placement in pay group E13 is possible, subject to the fulfillment of personal requirements. The Institute for Medical Informatics and Biometry (IMB) is part of the Carl Gustav Carus Faculty of Medicine at TU Dresden. The institute’s research focuses on medical biometrics, bioinformatics, systems biology/medicine, including mathematical modelling, as well as medical informatics. In addition to these scientific activities, the IMB offers various services (e.g., consulting and education programs in the field of medical data science) for faculty and students at the Faculty of Medicine and the University Hospital. The position is part of the interdisciplinary research project “Virtual niche: Computational modelling and simulation of spatio-temporal dynamics of hematopoietic stem cells in their local microenvironment” funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). The core objective of the project is the development and application of a mathematical model that describes the spatio-temporal organization of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in their local growth environment within the bone marrow. The goal of gaining a better understanding of the underlying processes is of central importance both for open questions in basic stem cell biology and for future medical applications. Your responsibilities: Development of mathematical models to describe cellular dynamics Implementation of the models in a suitable programming environment Simulation of cellular dynamics within complex 3D structures Application of the computer model as a virtual bridge between in vitro and in vivo studies Systemic analysis and interpretation of experimental data in the context of complex biological interactions Close interdisciplinary collaboration with experimental teams at TU Dresden and external partner laboratories Your Profil: University degree (M.Sc., Diplom, or equivalent) in mathematics, physics, computer science, engineering (with biological/biotechnological focus) or a related field Very good or excellent academic record Strong interest in interdisciplinary work, particularly in the application of mathematical and computational methods in biology and medicine Solid programming experience (e.g. in the statistical software R or Python) Knowledge of (stem) cell biology and experience in mathematical modelling are advantageous Reliability, creativity, flexibility, and the ability to work well in a team A cooperative, self-motivated, and goal-oriented work style Very good English skills We offer: Compensation: Based on the TV-L Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the Federal States in pay grade E13 , plus an annual bonus, provided you meet the personal requirements Vacation: 30 days of paid vacation Professional Development: Extensive internal and external training and development opportunities to continuously strengthen your skills Company Culture: We value transparency, team spirit, and shared success. Celebrate with us at company gatherings or sporting events like the Rewe Team Challenge. Mobility: A subsidy for a job ticket to make your commute eco-friendly and convenient Health: We promote your well-being with modern fitness and exercise programs at our health center, mental health programs, and a comprehensive workplace health management program. Shopping benefits: Take advantage of employee discounts at our clinic pharmacy, exclusive corporate benefits, and other shopping portals. linkedin:4478501795.title: Promovendus digi-, data- en AI-competenties
linkedin:4478501795.desc: De zorg van morgen wordt steeds digitaler. Maar technologie werkt pas als zorgprofessionals ermee kunnen werken. Hoe leren studenten en professionals digi-, data- en AI-competenties? En hoe bereiden we hen voor op een snel veranderende digitale wereld? Dat onderzoek jij! Aantal uur: 28 • 36 uur per week Werklocatie: Beide locaties Amsterdam UMC Contractvorm: Bepaalde tijd Salaris: € 3.217 - € 4.077 Reageer tot en met: 2 november 2026 Wat ga je doen? Je combineert literatuuronderzoek met het ontwikkelen en evalueren van leertrajecten voor (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Je werkzaamheden bestaan uit: Je brengt de wetenschappelijke literatuur en de meest recente inzichten op het gebied van digi-, data- en AI-competenties en leren en ontwikkelen in kaart. Je schrijft een algemeen onderzoeksplan en werkt dit uit in deelstudies, inclusief de benodigde ethische goedkeuringen. Je onderzoekt modellen, methoden en technieken voor een leven lang ontwikkelen. Daarbij kijk je bijvoorbeeld naar transfer of training, simulatieleren en werkplekleren om tot schaalbare oplossingen te komen. Je ontwikkelt en evalueert leertrajecten, waaronder pilots, voor (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Je adviseert waar nodig projecten en programma's binnen Amsterdam UMC die aansluiten bij jouw onderzoek. Daarnaast schrijf je wetenschappelijke artikelen voor nationale en internationale tijdschriften. Je bundelt je onderzoeksresultaten uiteindelijk in een proefschrift en presenteert je bevindingen op nationale en internationale congressen. Ook draag je beperkt bij aan onderwijs en opleiden van studenten en medewerkers, voor zover dit aansluit bij jouw onderzoek. Wat neem je mee? We nodigen je uit om te solliciteren als je een van de volgende opleidingen hebt afgerond: Een (research)master onderwijskunde, met affiniteit met en bij voorkeur ervaring in de gezondheidszorg. Of: Een (research)master gezondheidswetenschappen, aangevuld met aantoonbare didactische ervaring of scholing. Daarnaast herken je jezelf in het volgende profiel: Je hebt aantoonbare affiniteit met onderzoek en ervaring met kwalitatieve en kwantitatieve onderzoeksmethoden. Je hebt interesse in digitalisering, data en AI in de zorg en in didactische principes zoals simulatieleren en werkplekleren, of je wilt je hierin verder verdiepen. Je bent analytisch sterk, zelfstandig en nieuwsgierig. Ook heb je het doorzettingsvermogen om een promotietraject succesvol af te ronden. Je beheerst het Nederlands en Engels goed, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Je kunt complexe onderwerpen helder uitleggen. Ervaring met lesgeven of begeleiden is een pré. Je werkt graag samen, maar kunt ook zelfstandig aan de slag. Wat bieden we jou? Je treedt in dienst bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Een contract voor de duur van 12 maanden, met de intentie te verlengen tot een totaal van vier jaar. Voor deze vacature geldt de Richtlijn Promovendi. Inschaling in salarisschaal OIO: € 3.217 tot € 4.077 bruto bij een fulltime dienstverband (afhankelijk van ervaring). Daarnaast ontvang je 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering. Bereken hier jouw netto salaris. Mogelijkheid tot hybride werken, waarbij je minimaal twee dagen per week op locatie werkt. Vakantie-uren: 194,4 uur per jaar bij een fulltime dienstverband en de mogelijkheid om uren bij te sparen. 100% OV-vergoeding. Kom je lopend, fietsend of met de auto? Dan ontvang je een vergoeding van €0,21 per km (voor de auto geldt een maximum van 40 km enkele reis). Kom je op de fiets? Maak gebruik van onze goede fietsregeling. Pensioenopbouw bij BeFrank, een modern, begrijpelijk en eerlijk geprijsd pensioen. Bekijk deze video met meer informatie over de indiensttreding bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Waar ga je werken ? Je werkt bij het Teaching & Learning Centre (TLC) van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de UvA, bij Amsterdam UMC, locatie AMC, aan de Meibergdreef. Je maakt deel uit van het onderzoeksteam, een van de vier teams binnen het TLC. Dit kleine team bestaat uit onderwijskundig onderzoekers en innovators die samenwerken aan onderwijsvernieuwing en onderzoek. Daarnaast werk je inhoudelijk samen met het projectteam dat de leerpaden voor digi-, data- en AI-vaardigheden binnen Amsterdam UMC ontwikkelt en in de praktijk brengt. Het TLC is het expertisecentrum voor hoger onderwijs van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de UvA. Het ondersteunt de opleidingen Geneeskunde en Medische informatiekunde bij het verzorgen van hoogwaardig onderwijs. Onderwijskundig adviseurs, medical educators, trainers, onderzoekers en innovators werken er samen aan het verbeteren van onderwijs en opleiden. Het TLC maakt deel uit van de kerntaak Onderwijs & Opleiden van Amsterdam UMC en draagt bij aan de ontwikkeling van studenten en (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Binnen het team heerst een open en samenwerkingsgerichte cultuur. Kennis delen en samen leren staan centraal. Je werkt ook nauw samen met onderzoekers van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de VU en met andere afdelingen binnen Amsterdam UMC. Zo draag je bij aan een groeiende community op het gebied van onderwijsonderzoek. Wat ga je onderzoeken? Je onderzoekt welke digi-, data- en AI-competenties huidige en toekomstige zorgprofessionals nodig hebben. Je brengt in kaart welke competenties al goed zijn ontwikkeld en waar nog hiaten of overlap bestaan. Op basis daarvan ontwikkel je een breed, evidence-based competentieraamwerk. Je doet voorstellen om deze competenties efficiënt te integreren in het continuüm van onderwijs en opleiden. Waar mogelijk evalueer je bestaande en nieuwe leerinterventies die aansluiten op (onderdelen van) het raamwerk. Daarbij kijk je niet alleen naar het directe leerrendement, maar ook naar de vraag of professionals de competenties op langere termijn behouden en toepassen. Je onderzoek sluit aan bij een groter project binnen Amsterdam UMC. Daarin ontwerpen, ontwikkelen en testen we al enkele jaren leerpaden voor verschillende doelgroepen. De ontwikkelde producten, zoals de ontwerpmethodiek, het eerste competentiemodel en het evaluatieproces, vormen de basis voor jouw onderzoek. Tegelijkertijd biedt deze context volop ruimte om nieuwe onderzoeksvragen te verkennen. Wil je alvast meer weten over de verschillende fases binnen het PhD-traject? Op deze pagina lees je hierover meer informatie. Laten we kennismaken De beoogde startdatum is zo snel mogelijk, in overleg. Heb je interesse? Stuur dan je motivatiebrief en cv, aangevuld met een publicatielijst indien relevant. De eerste ronde sollicitatiegesprekken vindt plaats in de week van maandag 16 november 2026 . Tijdens deze gesprekken maak je kennis met de vice-decaan Onderwijs van de UvA, het hoofd van het TLC en de coördinerend onderzoeker van het onderzoeksteam. We vragen je om hier alvast rekening mee te houden. Heb je nog vragen? Voor inhoudelijke informatie over deze vacature kun je terecht bij Tom Broens , h oofd TLC, via t.h.broens@amsterdamumc.nl . Een referentiecheck en screening kunnen onderdeel zijn van de procedure. Lees hier wat dit inhoudt. Kom je bij ons in dienst, dan vragen we een VOG (Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag). Interne kandidaten krijgen, bij gelijke geschiktheid, voorrang op externe kandidaten. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

linkedin:4479030385.desc: Craft: Technology & Development Job Description: AI/ML Research Engineer Internship - 2027 About AI Labs at King’s AI Center of Excellence: Join AI Labs, an applied research team within King’s AI Center of Excellence, where innovation and collaboration come together to tackle complex modeling challenges and explore the latest advances in machine learning. You will gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced environment, developing solutions with real-world impact across our products and services. linkedin:4479022782.loc: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
linkedin:4479022782.desc: Job Description Are you interested in exploring the following questions? How are artificial intelligence (AI) and automation reshaping individuals' transitions to entrepreneurship? How do individuals' skills, experience, and technological readiness influence the types of businesses they create and their subsequent performance? How do these patterns vary across countries and institutional contexts? DTU Entrepreneurship invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship as part of an international research project entitled The New Landscape of Necessity Entrepreneurship: Understanding Entrepreneurial Transitions in an Era of AI- and Automation-Driven Labor Market Disruption . The project investigates how AI and automation reshape entrepreneurial transitions, with particular attention to individuals who start businesses following unemployment. The PhD candidate will join an international research team involving Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Professor Marc Gruber at École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland, and Professor John C. Dencker at Northeastern University, USA. Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF), the project combines large-scale surveys, Danish administrative registry data, and qualitative interviews across Denmark, Switzerland, and Greece. The position offers an opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge entrepreneurship research, work with rich international datasets, and collaborate with leading scholars in the field. Responsibilities And Qualifications Your primary responsibility will be to conduct high-quality research within the international project, with opportunities to develop your own research questions within its overall scope. Your tasks will include: Developing research questions and theoretical frameworks concerning entrepreneurship, human capital, AI, and labor market transitions. Applying quantitative and qualitative research methods to investigate entrepreneurial transitions and outcomes. Collecting, managing, and analyzing quantitative data, including large-scale surveys and Danish registry data. Contributing to the design and implementation of surveys and qualitative interviews in collaboration with international research partners. Preparing research papers for submission to leading international academic journals. Presenting research findings at international conferences and contributing to dissemination activities targeting policymakers and other stakeholders. Collaborating with researchers at DTU, EPFL, Northeastern University, and other project partners. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in entrepreneurship research and technological change. We expect you to have: A Master’s degree. A strong interest in developing quantitative research and analytical skills. Excellent written and spoken English communication skills. The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment. The following qualifications would be considered an advantage, but are not required: Experience working with large-scale datasets, registry data, or longitudinal data. Experience with statistical software such as Stata or R, and familiarity with econometric techniques, including regression analysis and panel data methods. Experience with survey design, qualitative interviewing, or mixed-methods research. You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . Assessment The assessment of applicants will be conducted by Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou, who will serve as the principal supervisor. We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The expected starting date is as soon as possible or as agreed with the successful candidate. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou, DTU Entrepreneurship, Technical University of Denmark, at argnik@dtu.dk . You can read more about DTU Entrepreneurship at www.entrepreneurship.dtu.dk . If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 8 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time) . Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file . The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter) Curriculum vitae Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. DTU Entrepreneurship is amongst the leading international entities in technology entrepreneurship and helps develop an entrepreneurial culture across DTU. As part of a dynamic and evolving ecosystem, we combine practice-oriented education and research in entrepreneurship with real start-up opportunities from all DTU departments. With rigorous research at its core, the Center builds the entrepreneurial capabilities of students, industry leaders, academics and policymakers to address unsolved problems, and together create new knowledge, methodologies and initiatives. We enable ethically minded entrepreneurs to build solutions that benefit people, society and the world. The Center experiments with new entrepreneurial methodologies and activities to push boundaries within research and education. DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829 DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

linkedin:4479063185.title: Promovendus klinisch redeneren en AI: leren in een gesimuleerde zorgwereld
linkedin:4479063185.desc: Fascineert het je hoe artsen leren redeneren? En wil je meebouwen aan de toekomst van medisch onderwijs, met simulatie, virtuele patiënten en AI? Dan nodigen we je uit als promovendus om te onderzoeken hoe we klinisch redeneren kunnen trainen als de 'echte' patiënt niet altijd binnen handbereik is. Aantal uur: 28 • 36 uur per week Werklocatie: Locatie VUmc Contractvorm: Bepaalde tijd Salaris: € 3.217 - € 4.077 Reageer tot en met: 26 oktober 2026 Wat ga je doen? Je exploreert de literatuur op de huidige state-of-the-art rond bovenstaande onderwerpen. Je schrijft een algemeen onderzoeksplan en plannen voor deelstudies met bijbehorende ethische goedkeuringen. Je onderzoekt welke onderdelen van klinisch redeneren (zoals het toepassen van fundamentele kennis, het verzamelen van informatie, het afwegen van diagnoses en het formuleren van beleid) zich lenen voor welke vorm van simulatie, en welke taken juist de echte patiënt vragen. Je onderzoekt hoe AI, zoals LLM-gebaseerde chatbots, kan helpen bij het genereren van realistische casuïstiek op maat, het simuleren van patiënten en het geven van feedback op het redeneerproces, en hoe betrouwbaar en onderwijskundig effectief dat is. Je werkt hierbij samen met docenten en studenten, bijvoorbeeld in het Klinisch Trainingscentrum, de Living Library en de studentenpoli. Samen met onderwijskundigen en docenten in het Amsterdam UMC die al ervaring opdoen met LLM-gebaseerde chatbots in het onderwijs, ontwikkel en evalueer je (pilot)onderwijs voor coassistenten. Je verzamelt en analyseert data uit onder andere experimentele studies, met kwalitatieve en kwantitatieve methoden, en interpreteert de bevindingen in de context van het medisch onderwijs. Je schrijft wetenschappelijke artikelen voor (inter)nationale tijdschriften en brengt de resultaten uiteindelijk samen in jouw proefschrift. Je presenteert jouw bevindingen op nationale en internationale congressen en bouwt zo aan een sterk academisch profiel en netwerk. Je volgt onder andere cursussen vanuit de Doctoral School Amsterdam UMC die aansluiten bij het project en bij jouw eigen ambities, en krijgt de mogelijkheid om ervaring op te doen in het verzorgen van onderwijs en het begeleiden van studenten. Wat neem je mee? Je hebt een afgeronde (research)master in onderwijskunde, cognitieve psychologie, gezondheidswetenschappen, geneeskunde, biomedische wetenschappen, informatiekunde of een vergelijkbaar vakgebied; Je hebt affiniteit met onderzoek. Ervaring met onderzoek waarbij je gebruik hebt gemaakt van kwalitatieve en/of kwantitatieve onderzoeksmethoden is een pré; Interesse in klinisch redeneren, medisch onderwijs, simulatieleren en de rol van AI in de zorg en het onderwijs, en de nieuwsgierigheid om je hier verder in te verdiepen; Je bent analytisch sterk, zelfstandig en kritisch, en je hebt het doorzettingsvermogen om een promotietraject tot een goed einde te brengen; Je kunt complexe materie helder overbrengen; ervaring met onderwijs of begeleiden is een plus; Je bent een teamspeler die zowel zelfstandig als binnen een groot multidisciplinair team (artsen, psychologen, onderwijskundigen en technici) kan werken; Je beheerst het Nederlands en Engels uitstekend, zowel schriftelijk als mondeling. Wat bieden we jou? Je treedt in dienst bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. De startdatum is zo snel mogelijk. Een contract voor de duur van 12 maanden, met de intentie te verlengen tot een totaal van vier jaar. Voor deze vacature geldt de Richtlijn Promovendi. Inschaling in salarisschaal OIO: € 3.217 tot € 4.077 bruto bij een fulltime dienstverband (afhankelijk van ervaring). Artsen worden ingeschaald in salarisschaal 10: € 3.724 tot € 5.867 bruto bij een fulltime dienstverband (afhankelijk van ervaring). Daarnaast ontvang je 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering. Bereken hier jouw netto salaris. Vakantie-uren: 194,4 uur per jaar bij een fulltime dienstverband en de mogelijkheid om uren bij te sparen. 100% OV-vergoeding. Kom je lopend, fietsend of met de auto? Dan ontvang je een vergoeding van €0,21 per km (voor de auto geldt een maximum van 40 km enkele reis). Kom je op de fiets? Maak gebruik van onze goede fietsregeling. Pensioenopbouw bij BeFrank, een modern, begrijpelijk en eerlijk geprijsd pensioen. Bekijk deze video met meer informatie over de indiensttreding bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Waar ga je werken ? Je maakt deel uit van het team Onderzoek van Onderwijs binnen de Faculteit Geneeskunde VU. Daarnaast neem je actief deel aan het netwerk i.o. voor onderzoek van onderwijs binnen Amsterdam UMC. Amsterdam UMC Research BV Amsterdam UMC Research BV ondersteunt wetenschappelijk onderzoek zonder winstoogmerk. Hiermee voorzien we onderzoekers in alles wat ze nodig hebben om te kunnen excelleren. Zo bieden onze principal investigators (PI's) en projectleiders begeleiding op het gebied van projectbeheer, finance en human resources. Bij medisch-wetenschappelijke onderzoeksprojecten wordt daarnaast ook ondersteuning op juridisch vlak geboden. Bekijk de video voor meer informatie. Wat ga je onderzoeken? Klinisch redeneren is de kern van het artsenvak: het vermogen om uit het patiëntverhaal, de uitgevraagde klachten, het lichamelijk onderzoek en onderzoeksuitslagen de juiste diagnose en het juiste plan te destilleren. Het is geen losse vaardigheid, maar een samenspel van veel onderdelen: fundamentele (bio)medische kennis, het verzamelen van informatie, het afwegen van diagnoses en het opstellen van beleid. Tijdens de coschappen leren geneeskundestudenten dit door te observeren, te oefenen met medestudenten en simulatiepatiënten, maar bovenal door dit daadwerkelijk uit te voeren bij de patiënt. Maar juist die leeromgeving staat onder druk. Door o.a. hoge werkdruk, fusies van ziekenhuizen, beperkte financiële ruimte, uitplaatsing naar zelfstandige behandelcentra (ZBC’s) en verplaatsing van zorg naar de eerste lijn neemt de opleidingscapaciteit van coassistenten af. Daardoor is het voor coassistenten steeds lastiger om voldoende, gevarieerde en veilige oefenmomenten met echte patiënten te krijgen. Terwijl we juist die momenten nodig hebben om artsen goed op te leiden in klinisch redeneren. Simulatie en virtuele patiënten bieden een veelbelovend alternatief om studenten in de geneeskundeopleiding voor te bereiden op het zelfstandig zien van patiënten: studenten kunnen op hun eigen niveau veilig oefenen met een breed scala aan casuïstiek, zonder risico voor patiënten, en met directe feedback. AI maakt dat nu schaalbaar. Denk aan taalmodellen die realistische patiëntcasuïstiek genereren op maat van de student, die als virtuele patiënt een anamnese kan laten afnemen, of die als tutor kan meedenken en feedback geven op het redeneerproces zelf. Maar belangrijke vragen zijn nog onbeantwoord. Welke onderdelen van klinisch redeneren leer je goed in welke vorm van simulatie (van een virtuele patiënt achter een scherm, een simulatiepatiënt van vlees en bloed, tot een teamsimulatie met acteurs), en welke leer je het best bij een ‘echte’ patiënt? Hoe realistisch en betrouwbaar is de met behulp van AI gegenereerde casuïstiek? En hoe zorgen we dat studenten zowel leren klinisch redeneren mét AI als zélf kritisch blijven redeneren? Daar ga jij als promovendus onderzoek naar doen. Laten we kennismaken Let op: voeg bij je sollicitatie ook jouw publicatielijst mee aan het einde van jouw motivatiebrief of cv (indien relevant). De eerste ronde sollicitatiegesprekken starten in de week van 26 oktober . Deze gesprekken worden gehouden met de vice-decaan onderwijs FdG VU en het hoofd onderzoek van onderwijs FdG VU. Heb je nog vragen? Voor inhoudelijke informatie over deze vacature kun je terecht bij Martine de Bruijne , vice-decaan onderwijs FdG VU, via mc.debruyne@amsterdamumc.nl . Een referentiecheck en screening kunnen onderdeel zijn van de procedure. Kom je bij ons in dienst, dan vragen we voor een aantal functiegroepen standaard een VOG (Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag). Bekijk wat het inhoudt en of het voor jouw functie van toepassing is. Interne kandidaten krijgen, bij gelijke geschiktheid, voorrang op externe kandidaten. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

linkedin:4479018891.title: PhD position: modeling menopause-related heart rhythm disorders
linkedin:4479018891.desc: Job Description Menopause induces profound electrical and structural changes in the heart, yet the mechanisms driving this transition, and the reasons it dramatically increases the risk of heart rhythm disorders in women, remain largely unexplored. In this PhD project, you will play a central role in uncovering these mechanisms by developing advanced, multi‑scale computational models of atrial electrophysiology. You will work with one of the most comprehensive and unique datasets available worldwide: high‑resolution intra‑operative electrical mapping data recorded directly from the human atria during cardiac surgery, combined with ECG, PPG, hormone profiles, and continuous vital signs. All data is collected within Erasmus MC, giving you direct access to clinicians, engineers, and the surgical team collecting the data. This means you will not rely on synthetic or incomplete datasets but you will build models grounded in rich, real-world physiology. Your task is to transform these multimodal datasets into patient‑specific “digital twins” that simulate how atrial electrophysiology evolves across the menopausal transition. You will design and calibrate mechanistic models at the cellular, tissue, and organ scale; develop numerical methods and optimization pipelines; and run large-scale simulations to reconstruct remodeling trajectories and identify the critical “breaking points” that lead to arrhythmias such as sinus node dysfunction and atrial fibrillation. The mechanistic insights and model outputs you generate will directly feed into the women‑specific arrhythmia detection algorithms developed by our industrial partner. Your work will therefore have a clear translational pathway toward real‑world digital health solutions. Beyond modeling, you will contribute to algorithm development for arrhythmia prediction and collaborate closely with clinical researchers during patient recruitment and data collection. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys combining computational modeling, physiology, and real clinical data. Your work will directly advance women‑specific arrhythmia detection and care, making a scientific impact that is both academically significant and clinically meaningful. “What I enjoy most is seeing how mathematical models can reveal mechanisms that cannot be directly observed from data.” - team member The position will be available by Q4 2026. The project is funded by Health-Holland. Work environment You will conduct your research within the Translational Electrophysiology Unit of the Department of Cardiology at Erasmus MC. The group is internationally recognized for its work on cardiac electrophysiology and collaborates closely with the Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery and multiple research groups at TU Delft. You will join a multidisciplinary, inclusive, and collegial team of clinicians, engineers, and scientists who work together to understand and treat cardiac arrhythmias. The environment is dynamic, supportive, and rich in opportunities for scientific growth. Qualifications And Skills We are looking for a motivated researcher with: A MSc or MEng degree in Mathematics, Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Computational Science, or a related field. Strong interest in computational modeling, simulations, or mathematical physiology. Experience with dynamical systems, numerical simulation, or finite‑element–based modeling approaches is a strong plus. Programming experience (preferably Python, but other languages are also a plus). Affinity with clinical or patient‑related research. Excellent communication skills and ability to work in a multidisciplinary team. Strong analytical mindset and enthusiasm for scientific discovery. Terms of employment A full‑time, 4‑year PhD position. A gross monthly salary between € 3.217,- and € 4.077,- (scale OIO) based on a full-time workweek of 36 hours. A salary increase of 3.5% from May 2027, according to the collective labor agreement (CLA). Excellent fringe benefits, such as a 13th month that is already paid out in November and an individual travel expense package. Pension insurance with ABP. We take care of approximately 2/3 of the monthly contribution. Special benefits, such as an incompany physiotherapist and bicycle repairer. And there is also a gym where you can work on your fitness after work. A supportive team and excellent supervision. Opportunities to attend international conferences and courses. A dynamic research environment at the largest academic medical center in the Netherlands. More information Make this job your next career move! Apply now using the application button. For more information about the role, please contact Dr. Vehpi Yildirim, Department of Cardiology (mail (mailto:v.yildirim@erasmusmc.nl)or +31 (0)6 812 496 74), or Prof. Dr. Natasja de Groot, Department of Cardiology, Erasmus MC via mail (mailto:n.m.s.degroot@erasmusmc.nl).

linkedin:4468727081.title: Doctoral Researcher, MSCA Doctoral Network position “Electric solar wind sail mission design”
linkedin:4468727081.desc: MSCA Doctoral Network position “Electric solar wind sail mission design” We are now looking for two (2) Doctoral Researchers. This PhD topic is part of the “Electric solar wind sail doctors” (E-Sailors) network, funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network Programme. The E-Sailors network is designed to train the next generation of Electric solar wind sail (E-sail) scientists, developers and advocates. This particular Doctoral Researcher (DR) will work with in-orbit results of on-going missions, such as Foresail-1 p developed by Aalto University with the E-sail payload from the Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI), as well as the DR will develop new and improved in-orbit E-sail experiments for future missions in lunar orbit and deep space. The DR will be enrolled at and hosted by Aalto University, Finland, with the main supervisor Jaan Praks, co-hosted by the FMI with the E-sail researcher Dr. Petri Toivanen. Research field : Space technology, payload development Supervisor : Jaan Praks Offered by : Aalto University, School of Electrical Engineering General Description Of Programme And Host The Electric solar wind Sail doctors (E-Sailors) is a challenge-based Doctoral Network that aims to bring Electric solar wind sail (E-sail) from low Earth orbit (LEO) demonstration missions to the operational environment of the solar wind. It is delivered by 8 universities in cooperation with FMI, where E-sail was invented, and 4 companies. E-sail is a highly innovative and potentially disruptive propellantless propulsion system. An operational E-sail consists of hair-thin and kilometres-long wires, or tethers, which are charged at a high voltage creating an electrostatic sheath (electric sail) which deflects solar wind particles and generates the propulsive effect in interplanetary environment. Successful and rapid development and deployment of the technology will ensure EU's leadership in the exploration and exploitation of deep space, the next commercial space frontier. The programme is designed to achieve the following training objectives for our doctoral researchers: Equip them with core scientific skills and specialised knowledge in designing experiments for demonstrating space technologies and developing space missions; Provide them with a wide range of transferrable skills, such as Open Science and FAIR, communicating science to public, advocacy, networking etc.; Develop their business and entrepreneurship skills, such as IPR management, preliminary business planning, pitching to investors, starting start-ups. Aalto University is a leading Finnish university combining science, technology, design, and business to foster innovation and multidisciplinary research. The Aalto Space Lab is a comprehensive facility dedicated to the development, integration, and qualification of small satellites and space payloads. The laboratory features an advanced electronics development environment equipped for precision soldering, calibration, functional testing, and sensor characterization. A dedicated cleanroom area supports the assembly and integration of flight hardware, ensuring high reliability and adherence to space standards. Adjacent to the electronics lab, the Space Technology Testing Laboratory provides an advanced thermal–vacuum facility that enables environmental testing of complete satellites and subsystems under simulated space conditions. linkedin:4476483317.desc: Are you passionate about human movement and developing clinical tools for understanding human movement disorders? Job Description Challenge: Over a quarter of a million people in the Netherlands alone have rheumatoid arthritis (RA) with a majority suffering from debilitating pain and inflammation that makes hand dexterity and work, at times, impossible. While anti-inflammatory and analgesic drugs are the main line of relief, new drugs and treatments are needed and being developed for long-term care. At the same time a major challenge in RA management is quantifying the effectiveness of treatments under real-world conditions. Change: We need technologies to measure and quantify changes in hand function due to daily life factors (sleep, stress, etc.…) and treatments/drugs in the home setting. These technologies would enable drug developers, physiotherapists and physicians to make objective and quantitative assessments regarding the effectiveness of treatments. Impact: Once we understand the effects of stressors and treatments on RA flare ups and hand function, clinicians will be able to more closely target treatments and plan daily routines that minimize pain and suffering from rheumatoid arthritis. We are seeking a PhD candidate for a 4-year contract to develop and apply computational models and video-based tools to capture hand movement and function with deployment in the home environment as the target. Furthermore, you will apply these tools to help us investigate the potential causes and timings of flare ups during patients’ daily lives. You will work primarily with video data, musculoskeletal models, and pose estimation algorithms. The models and algorithms you develop will be part of open source and data repositories affiliated with the broader research program and TU Delft’s commitment to Open Science. You will be an integral part of the ‘Care is coming home!’ program: a 5-year project executed by a large consortium consisting of 2 technical universities (TU Delft, UTwente), 6 hospitals (Amsterdam UMC, Erasmus MC, Leiden UMC, Maartenskliniek, Maastricht UMC, Radboud UMC), 13 companies (Able Human Motion, Biomex, Cue2Walk, DanuSports, Kinetic Analysis, Lode Holding, Madglove, ModelHealth, Moveshelf, Orikami, Sabender (Enterprising Company), Trinoma, VicarVision), 1 rehabilitation centre (Daan Theeuwes Centrum) and 5 patient organisations (Hersenletsel.nl, Hersenstichting, Parkinson Vereniging, ParkinsonNL, ReumaNederland). In total the program will encompass 9 PhDs and 5 postdocs to address the issue of translating health care to the home environment. This PhD position is hosted by the Biomechanical Engineering Department at TU Delft where you will be a part of both the Computational Biomechanics (Seth) and Neuromuscular Control (Mugge) Labs. In addition to research, there are many opportunities to develop your academic career by mentoring and teaching BSc/MSc students, presenting at international conferences, and participating in workshops/training and exchange programs abroad. Job requirements You Should Have MSc in engineering or similar discipline by the start date of the position Experience with mechanical modeling and simulation Experience in computer programming/scripting (e.g., C++, Python, Matlab, etc.) Experience collecting human experimental data (movement, video, or similar) Excellent written and oral communication skills in English The following aspects will help you stand out: Thriving in multidisciplinary environments Curiosity-driven and self-motivated working attitude Knowledge of biomechanical modeling, anatomy, vision-based motion capture, machine learning, control systems Keep in mind that this describes the background we imagine would best fit the role. linkedin:4479087828.title: PhD position: modeling menopause-related heart rhythm disorders
linkedin:4479087828.desc: Job Description Menopause induces profound electrical and structural changes in the heart, yet the mechanisms driving this transition, and the reasons it dramatically increases the risk of heart rhythm disorders in women, remain largely unexplored. In this PhD project, you will play a central role in uncovering these mechanisms by developing advanced, multi‑scale computational models of atrial electrophysiology. You will work with one of the most comprehensive and unique datasets available worldwide: high‑resolution intra‑operative electrical mapping data recorded directly from the human atria during cardiac surgery, combined with ECG, PPG, hormone profiles, and continuous vital signs. All data is collected within Erasmus MC, giving you direct access to clinicians, engineers, and the surgical team collecting the data. This means you will not rely on synthetic or incomplete datasets but you will build models grounded in rich, real-world physiology. Your task is to transform these multimodal datasets into patient‑specific “digital twins” that simulate how atrial electrophysiology evolves across the menopausal transition. You will design and calibrate mechanistic models at the cellular, tissue, and organ scale; develop numerical methods and optimization pipelines; and run large-scale simulations to reconstruct remodeling trajectories and identify the critical “breaking points” that lead to arrhythmias such as sinus node dysfunction and atrial fibrillation. The mechanistic insights and model outputs you generate will directly feed into the women‑specific arrhythmia detection algorithms developed by our industrial partner. Your work will therefore have a clear translational pathway toward real‑world digital health solutions. Beyond modeling, you will contribute to algorithm development for arrhythmia prediction and collaborate closely with clinical researchers during patient recruitment and data collection. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys combining computational modeling, physiology, and real clinical data. Your work will directly advance women‑specific arrhythmia detection and care, making a scientific impact that is both academically significant and clinically meaningful. “What I enjoy most is seeing how mathematical models can reveal mechanisms that cannot be directly observed from data.” - team member The position will be available by Q4 2026. The project is funded by Health-Holland.

linkedin:4479215663.desc: Career at WUR About Us Plenty of variety and challenges Pleasant working atmosphere Time for personal development Proper work-life balance Internationally leading Your job Have you ever wondered how we can ensure that climate mitigation and adaptation policies are fair, coherent, and effective? Are you interested in applying state-of-the-art impact evaluation techniques to analyze how climate policies affect land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity? Do you good communication skills in Spanish? Then this might be your next step! Climate change mitigation and adaptation in agriculture and forestry represent a “wicked problem”, shaped by uncertainty, conflicting objectives, institutional fragmentation and time pressure. While the EU has set ambitious climate targets for 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050, progress in agriculture and forestry remains insufficient and current policy frameworks have not yet resulted in significant climate mitigation and adaptation results, or generated the systemic transformation needed. This PhD position is part of the EU-Horizon project “ Evidence-based pathways towards fair, coherent and effective climate policies for Europe’s agriculture and forestry (PolicyForClimate) ”, which will develop tools and frameworks to enable policymakers and other stakeholders to design fair, coherent, and effective climate mitigation and adaptation policies in the EU. The project will use AI-assisted evidence synthesis, a policy-lab approach, and embedded case studies to offer a continuously updated evidence base on policy impacts, trade-offs, synergies, and spillovers. Your research will focus on developing, applying, and validating a novel mixed-methods framework for ex-post impact evaluation of climate policies in forestry and agricultural landscapes. By combining state-of-the-art econometric techniques with qualitative participatory approaches, you will empirically analyze how climate policies have affected land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity metrics. This will require conducting systematic reviews on existing impact evaluation frameworks, run workshops and focus group discussions with various stakeholders, collect, combine, and analyze farm-level primary data and secondary spatially explicit data. Start date: February 2027. Your Duties And Responsibilities Include Conduct systematic literature reviews and workshops to develop a mixed-methods ex-post impact evaluation framework for climate policies; Apply rigorous econometric methods together with qualitative assessments, particularly from policy sciences, to evaluate the impact of specific climate policies on land cover, carbon, and biodiversity metrics; Conduct focus group discussions with various stakeholders in the EU to validate the proposed impact evaluation framework and results from the empirical analyses; Write research papers and present research findings at international academic conferences; Collaborate with our research partners and contribute to the dissemination of project results. You will work here You will be based at the Forest and Nature Conservation Policy Group (FNP) at Wageningen University . The FNP group focuses on the political, socio-economic and cultural dimensions of forests and nature. Our research addresses major challenges including biodiversity conservation, deforestation, forest transitions, climate change and landscape management in both the Global North and Global South. You will be jointly supervised by Dr. Jorge Sellare and Prof. Bas Arts from Wageningen University (WU-FNP), and by Dr. Dario Schulz (EFI) in the research group headed by Sven Wunder. Your qualities We are looking for a researcher with a strong interest in climate adaptation and mitigation policies and in exploring the underlying causal mechanisms through which they affect land, GHG emissions, and biodiversity. You enjoy working with both quantitative and qualitative data and are motivated to conduct research that combines rigorous econometric analysis with qualitative assessments and with real-world challenges facing farmers and forest owners. Fieldwork in Spain will be an important component of the PhD project, so Spanish language skills are critical. You should be enthusiastic about working with farmers and able to spend time in rural areas of Spain under fieldwork conditions. You Also Possess a successfully completed MSc degree in agricultural economics, environmental economics, environmental policy, forestry or a closely related field; affinity with applied econometrics and / or qualitative mixed methods and an interest in developing your skills in both; knowledge of GIS and spatial data analysis is an asset; good skills with statistical software such as R, Stata or Python; very good communication skills in Spanish (min. level B2); For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level . linkedin:4478406768.title: Research Scientist, Doctoral Researcher, tree breeding
linkedin:4478406768.desc: We are looking for a doctoral researcher for a project "Thousand Ways to Die - evolutionary and molecular background of excessive early developmental mortality in Scots pine” realized jointly by the University of Helsinki and Luke. Job description The Doctoral Researcher will carry out doctoral research in accordance with the project’s research plan. The aim is to investigate the reproductive system of Scots pine and the high mortality of seed embryos during early developmental stages. The main research topics are inbreeding depression and possible self-incompatibility mechanisms affecting embryo viability. We will use advanced methods, such as spatial transcriptomics, to investigate gene expression in seeds under different conditions and at different developmental stages. We will also compare natural embryo development with somatic embryogenesis, as well as the factors affecting these. The aim is to understand how mutation, purifying selection and adaptive evolution influence embryo viability, which may improve seed quality and enhance forest regeneration. The Doctoral Researcher’s role in the project’s sub-studies will be determined partly by the person's skills and interests, as the project will employ also Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Helsinki. The project is being carried out jointly by the University of Helsinki and the Natural Resources Institute Finland. The Postdoctoral Researcher will be employed by Luke, while supervision related to the doctoral degree will be provided by the University of Helsinki (Professor Pyhäjärvi, https://www.helsinki.fi/en/researchgroups/forest-genomics). The selected person will apply separately to the university’s doctoral programme. The position requires regular on-site presence and participation in field and laboratory work. Field trials will be conducted at Haapastensyrjä in Loppi and at seed orchards, while laboratory work will take place in Helsinki and, for somatic embryogenesis, at Savonlinna. Our expectations of the applicant We expect applicants to hold a Master’s degree in a relevant field (for example, agriculture and forestry, biology or genetics). The position requires knowhow and/or an interest in evolutionary biology and molecular genetics, as well as laboratory skills. Experience with molecular biology methods, microscopy and plant tissue culture is an advantage. Bioinformatics and computational skills are also considered an asset. Due to the collaborative nature of the project, strong teamwork and communication skills are essential. Excellent written and spoken English is required. The position also requires the ability to participate in field measurements and sampling; therefore, a category AB driving licence is an advantage. Additional information Tuija Aronen Group Manager, Luke +358 29 532 4233 tuija.aronen@luke.fi Tanja Pyhäjärvi Professor, University of Helsinki +358 29 415 7976 tanja.pyhajarvi@helsinki.fi Apply by 27.10.2026 at 16.00 (4 pm EET)

linkedin:4472090457.title: PhD Position Continuum Two-Phase Flow Modelling of Piping in Dikes
linkedin:4472090457.desc: Develop advanced models to understand and predict piping and internal erosion in dikes. As a PhD researcher at TU Delft, you will connect fundamental fluid–soil interaction physics with computational modelling to contribute to safer flood defences. Job Description Internal erosion and piping are among the main failure mechanisms of clay–sand layered dikes and remain important challenges in flood risk management. Reliable numerical models can improve our understanding of how piping develops and help engineers assess and design safer, more reliable flood defence systems. In this PhD project, you will contribute to this challenge by advancing the modelling of particle transport and fluid–soil interaction in dikes. A key scientific challenge is to represent the complex interaction between soil particles and flowing water across different spatial and temporal scales, while keeping the models computationally efficient. The research builds on an Eulerian two-phase modelling approach previously applied to backward erosion piping. You will investigate how this approach can be further developed to capture the physical processes that govern pipe formation and progression, while connecting detailed modelling with larger-scale analyses. The goal of the project is to develop a robust and computationally efficient modelling framework that improves the prediction of piping in layered dikes. Your research will contribute to a better understanding of internal erosion and support the development of safer flood defence systems and more reliable flood risk assessments. Your Responsibilities As a PhD researcher, you will: Develop continuum-based two-phase models to predict internal erosion and pipe progression in clay-sand layered dikes. Derive constitutive modelling approaches from high-fidelity DNS-DEM data generated within the broader project consortium. Capture the multi-scale nature of pipe formation while maintaining computational efficiency, including the exploration of adaptive mesh refinement strategies. Disseminate research outcomes through scientific publications, conference presentations, and collaboration with researchers from relevant disciplines. Your work environment You will join the Offshore and Dredging Engineering group within the department of Maritime and Transport Technology of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. You will receive supervision and guidance while having the freedom to shape and develop your research. You will have access to well-equipped facilities, including: The hydraulic circuit. You will work in an open and collaborative environment where interdisciplinary teamwork, curiosity and scientific excellence are valued. The group works closely across fluid mechanics, soil mechanics, hydraulic engineering and ocean engineering, using various computational and experimental techniques, sharing knowledge and expertise to develop innovative solutions with meaningful societal impact. Please see our work for more information: Offshore and Dredging Engineering. Job Requirements You are highly motivated to translate fundamental flow and erosion physics into practically relevant scales through two-phase flow modelling. You are well organised, manage your time effectively and take initiative in a multidisciplinary research environment. You are results-oriented and enjoy working with researchers from different disciplines. Furthermore, you meet the following requirements: You have an MSc degree in a relevant field (Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Applied Physics, Process Technology, Civil Engineering or a closely related discipline) You have received training in multiphase flow physics, numerical methods, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), ideally complemented by application in your MSc thesis, research projects, or internships. Have excellent communication skills and command of English. Have affinity with teaching and guiding MSc students. Familiarity with Euler–Euler multiphase flow modelling and/or automatic mesh adaptation techniques is considered an advantage. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. linkedin:4479244418.title: Industrial PhD student: Kinetic modelling of catalytic hydrogen oxidation for hydrogen engines
linkedin:4479244418.desc: Industrial PhD student: Kinetic modelling of catalytic hydrogen oxidation for hydrogen engines TRATON is a group of strong brands with a shared mission: transforming transportation together to create the future of sustainable transport solutions. Within TRATON, we include MAN, Scania, Volkswagen Truck & Bus, and International. As part of a global team of industry experts, you get to think bigger, experience more, and reach further. Together, we have the power to transform transportation - Let´s make a difference together. Find out more: www.traton.com Our values – customer first, respect, team spirit, responsibility, and elimination of waste – are at the heart of everything we do. Introduction Join us as an industrial PhD student and contribute to the development of future hydrogen-fuelled heavy-duty vehicles by developing predictive kinetic models for catalytic hydrogen combustion. The research will bridge fundamental catalysis, experimental studies and engine-level simulations, with the long-term aim of enabling efficient hydrogen powertrains with ultra low emissions. Hydrogen internal combustion engines (H₂-ICE) with high-pressure direct injection offer high efficiency and power density but face challenges related to cold start and the need of carbon-based pilot fuels for ignition. Catalytic hydrogen oxidation over noble metals such as platinum could improve cold-start performance and enable hydrogen-only ignition concepts. Role Summary This role is a part of TRATON Group R&D, located in Södertälje, Sweden. The main focus of this Industrial PhD is the development and validation of kinetic models for hydrogen oxidation over noble-metal catalysts across a broad range of operating conditions and applications, including cold-start and in-cylinder conditions. You will also work closely with other PhD students and researchers to design and conduct relevant experimental studies supporting kinetic model development and validation, providing opportunities for hands-on experimental work in catalysis. The position will be part of PtHICE – Innovative ways to use platinum for zero emission hydrogen vehicles, a joint research project involving TRATON, Chalmers University of Technology, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Christian-Albrechts-University of Kiel, AVL List GmbH and Johnson Matthey. You will be employed by TRATON AB and affiliated with the Division of Chemical Engineering at Chalmers University of Technology, and work in close collaboration with academic and industrial partners. Job Responsibilities The work will involve all parts of a research project, from developing scientific hypotheses and analysing experimental data to kinetic model development, validation and application. Your main responsibilities will include: Develop and validate kinetic models for catalytic hydrogen oxidation based on experimental data, and apply them in 1D and 3D simulations under engine-relevant conditions, including cold start and catalytic-assisted hydrogen ignition. Collaborate with academic and industrial partners across experiments and modelling, and communicate research results through scientific publications and international conferences. Who You Are We welcome applicants from all backgrounds – your unique experience and perspectives is valuable to us. You should have an M.Sc. degree in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Engineering Physics, Applied Physics, or a related field, preferably with a background or strong interest in catalysis, chemical kinetics, reaction engineering or numerical modelling. You should be interested in understanding physical and chemical phenomena from experimental data and translating this knowledge into mathematical and numerical models. As a person, you are curious, energetic and collaborative, with a proactive mindset and a strong interest in learning and exploring new ideas. You enjoy working in a multidisciplinary team and contributing to a positive research environment. You should have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Swedish language skills are considered a merit but are not required. TRATON Offers We offer a dynamic and engaging workplace where collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement are part of everyday life. You will be part of a strong team environment that encourages knowledge sharing and close cooperation across functions. With a structured development plan and a wide range of training opportunities, TRATON supports your professional growth both locally and internationally. Benefits include access to our health center in mapor a wellness allowance, bonus, flexible working hours, and company car leasing.
