linkedin:4479717292.title: PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN- NL
linkedin:4479717292.desc: The Faculty of Science and Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research (LACDR) are looking for candidates for a PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN ANA-KIN is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme. Over the past two decades, small-molecule kinase inhibitors have transformed cancer therapy, yet nearly all of them target the highly conserved ATP-binding site, which limits selectivity and allows resistance to emerge. ANA-KIN aims to train a new generation of interdisciplinary researchers capable of redefining kinase drug discovery beyond the ATP paradigm, by developing the experimental and computational tools, modular assays and workflows needed to systematically target non-conserved regulatory interfaces, such as kinase dimerization and substrate-binding sites. Proof-of-concept will be demonstrated on three representative kinases: EGFR, BRAF and the understudied “dark” kinase LTK. ANA-KIN brings together 11 beneficiaries and 9 associated partners across Europe and the USA, including Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (coordinator), University of Crete, Goethe University Frankfurt, Saarland University, EPFL, CNRS, Pompeu Fabra University, VIB, KU Leuven, INSERM and Leiden University, together with industrial partners such as AstraZeneca, Novartis, Servier and Skylight Therapeutics. The network combines chemical biology, structural biophysics (single-molecule FRET, cryo-EM, nanodiscs), AI-driven drug design and cell biology in an integrated learn–design–test loop. Twelve Doctoral Candidates (DCs) will each pursue an individual research project, benefit from co-supervision across institutions and sectors, carry out two research secondments at partner organizations, and follow a structured network-wide training program covering scientific, transferable, open-science and entrepreneurial skills. In this PhD project (DC10, Work Package 3 – Discovery), you will develop deep-learning architectures that integrate text-mined, cheminformatic, and biophysical descriptors to predict interface binding, allosteric signatures and resistance liabilities of kinase ligands. The models will learn jointly across peptide and small-molecule modalities and will be used to generate hybrid peptidomimetic design hypotheses. You will translate these models into consortium-wide prioritisation dashboards that support hit triage and analogue selection in the discovery campaigns of ANA-KIN, and work in close reciprocal feedback with DC9 (Saarland University) on structure-based and machine-learning pipelines. Model predictions will be validated prospectively with the experimental partners in the network. The expected results are a resistance-aware AI workflow for non-ATP interface ligands, accompanied by public models, datasets and interpretable feature maps, and prospective design case studies demonstrating improved optimisation trajectories. To reinforce structural grounding and experimental validation, you will carry out two secondments: at VIB (Belgium, Prof. Ruslan Efremov; 4 months) to extract structural classes and conformational features from cryo-EM data and use them to refine model constraints, and at Skylight Therapeutics (Belgium, Dr. Joshua Salafsky; 3 months) to test model predictions using second-harmonic generation (SHG)-based conformational profiling. The project will be supervised by Prof. Gerard J.P. van Westen (Leiden University), with Prof. Ruslan Efremov and Dr. Joshua Salafsky as co-supervisors. What You Will Do Conduct original and novel research in deep learning, AI, and cheminformatics for kinase drug discovery; Develop, benchmark and openly share models, datasets and decision-support dashboards following FAIR and open-science principles; Collaborate closely with experimental and computational DCs in the network, and carry out two research secondments abroad (VIB and Skylight Therapeutics, Belgium); Publish and present scientific articles at international journals and conferences; Participate in the ANA-KIN network-wide training events, schools and outreach activities; Contribute to educational activities; Write a dissertation. What You Bring A MSc degree in Computer Science, AI, (Computational) Chemistry, Bioinformatics, Biopharmaceutical Sciences, or a relevant related field; Good knowledge of and experience with machine learning and deep-learning techniques (e.g. PyTorch); Good knowledge of and experience with cheminformatics and/or computational chemistry (e.g. RDKit, molecular descriptors, docking); Interest in structural biology, protein kinases and drug discovery; affinity with peptide or biophysical data is an advantage; Highly motivated to both perform foundational research and apply the developed methods to real-world problems; creative, ‘making things work’ mentality, independent, and communicative team player; Willingness to travel and to carry out research secondments at partner institutions abroad; Excellent programming skills (preferably Python); Good academic writing skills and interest in participating in educational activities; Excellent proficiency in English (oral and written). MSCA eligibility criteria At the date of recruitment, candidates must not have been awarded a doctoral degree; Mobility rule: candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the Netherlands for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the date of recruitment. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status are not taken into account. Where you will work Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research Our institute is a center of excellence for multidisciplinary research on drug discovery and development. Leiden University consistently ranks within the top-20 world-wide within the subject-based QS Ranking in Pharmacology and Pharmacy. At LACDR, we develop innovative scientific concepts in fundamental and translational research underlying the discovery and optimization of drugs, and personalized medicines. We aim to optimize the route to novel drugs that are both efficacious and safe, and therefore our research focuses on drug discovery and safety, bio-therapeutics, and systems biomedicine and pharmacology. State-of-the-art expertise and infrastructures ensure that we are strategically positioned in (inter)national collaborations, thus further strengthening the development of novel concepts and their application in a clinical and industry environment. Computational Drug Discovery Research in this group, headed by Gerard van Westen, focusses on computational methods integrated in different parts of the drug discovery process. More specifically, topics include innovative treatments for cancer, kinase and GPCR drug discovery, proteochemometrics, selectivity and polypharmacology modeling, allosteric modulation, drug resistance modeling, de novo molecular design, and novel methods in the domain of machine learning. For more information see: http://www.cddl.nl Research at our faculty The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is diverse, ranging from artificial intelligence, computer science, mathematics, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,700 staff and almost 6,000 students. We are located in the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry meet. For more information, see http://www.science.leidenuniv.nl. What We Offer We offer a full-time appointment for 48 months as a Doctoral Candidate within the MSCA Doctoral Network ANA-KIN, starting late 2026. The appointment is initially for one year; after a positive evaluation of the progress of the research, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended for the remaining period. Salary ranges from € 3.204,- tot € 4.051,- gross per month (pay scale P in accordance with the Collective Labor Agreement for Dutch Universities). Leiden University offers an attractive benefits package with additional holiday (8%) and end-of-year bonuses (8.3%), training and career development. Our individual choices model gives you some freedom to assemble your own set of terms and conditions. Candidates from outside the Netherlands may be eligible for a substantial tax break. All our PhD students are embedded in the Leiden University Graduate School of Science. Our graduate school offers several PhD training courses at three levels: professional courses, skills training and personal effectiveness. In addition, advanced courses to deepen scientific knowledge are offered by the research school. As an ANA-KIN Doctoral Candidate you will also follow the network’s training program, including summer schools, workshops and an industrial immersion workshop, and your progress will be monitored by a Thesis Advisory Committee including an independent mentor. What We Value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. linkedin:4478871053.title: PhD position on ‘Adaptive Privacy and Differential Privacy for Energy Data’
linkedin:4478871053.desc: PhD position on ‘Adaptive Privacy and Differential Privacy for Energy Data’ 1,0 FTE position for 4 years. The PhD candidate will be appointed for a period of 15 months. The appointment will be extended to 4 years when progress and performance are good. A PhD training program is part of the agreement. Vacancy number: FAC/BW/26087 The Project Can you help make energy data usable without giving away sensitive information? The energy transition in the Netherlands urgently requires upgrading of the electricity grid, for instance to accommodate solar panels, wind turbines, and electric vehicles. To efficiently plan and manage these upgrades, stakeholders such as grid operators, municipalities and energy communities need to share detailed data about electricity consumption, generation and grid operation. This data sharing however is prevented by concerns on the competitively sensitive nature and privacy of data, as it reveals detailed information about households, buildings and operational assets. Synthetic data generated by generative AI-models offers a promising alternative, but preserving statistical, temporal, and physical characteristics of real energy data while protecting sensitive information are major challenges. We are offering a PhD position in the SHARE project that addresses these challenges. Research challenges As a PhD candidate, you will develop methods for adaptive privacy protection of energy data , combining differential privacy, empirical privacy attacks and privacy–utility optimisation. Your research is part of the Adaptive Privacy and Legal Compliance work package in the SHARE project. More specifically, your challenges are to: Investigate how temporal patterns, spatial information, rare events and other distinctive features contribute to re-identification and inference risk. You will work with metrics such as uniqueness, entropy, attack success rates and time-series-specific indicators. Implement and study attacks such as membership inference, reconstruction, re-identification and attribute inference to understand where information leakage occurs in both original and synthetic datasets. Investigate methods that allocate stronger protection to sensitive components and lighter perturbation to lower-risk components, thereby preserving as much analytical utility as possible. Formulate privacy protection as an optimisation problem balancing formal privacy guarantees against statistical, temporal and physical utility requirements for energy-system applications. Collaborate closely with researchers at Radboud University, who develop physics-informed generative models for synthetic energy data, and investigate approaches such as differentially private training and post-generation privacy calibration. Work closely with distribution system operator Alliander and other consortium partners to evaluate whether the developed methods provide meaningful protection while retaining the information required for practical energy-system applications. Ultimately contribute to an open-source privacy layer for the SHARE toolbox. Requirements You hold, or will soon obtain, an MSc degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related discipline. You should have: a strong background in privacy-enhancing technologies, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity or statistical modelling; strong programming skills, particularly in Python; preferably, some familiarity with deep generative models (VAEs, GANs, diffusion models) and probabilistic modelling; good written and spoken English skills; knowledge of Dutch language preferred not mandatory. Salary The salary is determined in accordance with salary scale P of Appendix A of the Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities and ranges from € 3.204,-- gross per month upon commencement to € 4.051,-- gross per month in the fourth and final year, in case of full employment. The Open Universiteit provides good secondary benefits such as training, mobility, part-time employment and paid parental leave. Station The position is officially based in Heerlen. As part of the PhD project, you will mainly work at Radboud University in Nijmegen, where you will collaborate closely with the other researchers in the SHARE project. This setup enables close day-to-day collaboration with researchers working on machine learning, synthetic data and energy systems. You will be employed by Open Universiteit and supervised by Dr. Mina Alishahi as your primary supervisor, with Prof. dr. ir. Harald Vranken as co-supervisor. Information For more information about this vacancy you can contact: harald.vranken@ou.nl. Procedure Please apply to this position by sending an email to solliciteren@ou.nl, stating the vacancy number and including: your CV; a motivation letter; your MSc thesis or another representative piece of academic work, if available; contact details of two references. In your motivation letter, please briefly address the following three questions: Why are you interested in privacy-preserving machine learning and, in particular, this PhD project? Describe a research, thesis or programming project in which you worked with machine learning, privacy, cybersecurity, generative models or complex data. What was your own contribution? Provide a one-paragraph description of your MSc thesis, written for a reader outside your field. You will preferably start your employment on January 1st, 2027. Closing date: November 1st, 2026 Working at the Open University Working at the Open University means contributing to academic education for the most motivated students in the Netherlands and Flanders, as well as to scientific research with visible impact for people and society. With a broad range of bachelor’s and master’s programmes and short courses, the Open University makes lifelong learning accessible to everyone. There are no prior education requirements for bachelor’s programmes: anyone aged eighteen or older can enrol. Education is hybrid and flexible, available anytime and anywhere, at a pace that suits the student. The majority of the nearly 16,000 students combine their studies with work. This creates a valuable interaction: experiences and questions from professional practice enrich education and research and increase their societal relevance. It is therefore no coincidence that the Open University has ranked in the top three of the Dutch Keuzegids for universities for many years, and this year holds the number one position. In research, the university focuses on three central themes: healthcare, digitalisation and AI, and society and citizenship. Solutions to today’s challenges are sought across disciplinary boundaries and in collaboration with partners. The Open University employs approximately 800 staff members, has its main campus in Heerlen, and operates study centres in the Netherlands and Flanders. Its culture is people-centred, collaborative, and inclusive: an environment in which students, staff, and partners feel connected, with ample opportunities for personal development and a healthy work–life balance. Department of Computer Science You will be appointed within the Department of Computer Science of the Faculty of Science. The department’s research program “Towards high-quality and intelligent software” (2020–2025) consists of four research lines, focusing on: Techniques for quality assurance of software systems Software and computer system security, and privacy-by-design Responsible artificial intelligence, including methods and applications of AI Educational tools and computing education.

linkedin:4443351953.title: CIFRE - Intégration d’architectures de qubits de spin en silicium en technologie CMOS FDSOI avancée pour le calcul quantique (F/H)
linkedin:4443351953.desc: Chez STMicroelectronics, nous sommes convaincus que la technologie est un moteur d’innovation et a un impact positif pour les entreprises, les personnes et la société. En tant qu’acteur mondial des semiconducteurs, nos technologies de pointe et nos composants électroniques sont invisibles mais au cœur du monde d’aujourd’hui. Rejoindre ST, c’est intégrer une entreprise internationale riche de plus de 115 nationalités, présente dans 40 pays, et rassemblant plus de 50 000 talents passionnés et engagés, tous unis par la volonté de créer et d’inventer la technologie de demain. Innover demande bien plus que des compétences techniques : cela nécessite des personnes inspirantes, qui savent collaborer avec respect et enthousiasme. Des collaborateurs animés par la passion, prêts à remettre en question le statu quo, à faire avancer l’innovation et à révéler leur plein potentiel. Venez vivre cette aventure avec nous et contribuez à construire un futur plus intelligent et plus durable, en alliant responsabilité et innovation. Notre technologie commence avec vous. La course à la réalisation d’un ordinateur quantique démontrant la suprématie quantique s’intensifie, mobilisant de puissantes entreprises et de nombreux gouvernements, qui travaillent sur de multiples supports physiques pour encoder l’information quantique, tels que la supraconductivité, les ions piégés, le spin de l’électron dans le silicium ou encore la photonique. Dans cette compétition, ST et QUOBLY peuvent tirer parti de la technologie FDSOI, qui offre un environnement idéal pour isoler et manipuler le spin de l’électron utilisé dans les algorithmes quantiques. Pendant les 3 années de recherche, le doctorant devra étudier et proposer une architecture de dispositif basée sur la technologie CMOS FDSOI permettant de supporter des qubits en silicium à base de spin pour le calcul quantique. Les principaux axes de développement seront : l’architecture du dispositif (simulation 3D et réalisation des dispositifs sur silicium), l’analyse des matériaux et la caractérisation cryogénique. A propos de vos missions Réaliser une étude bibliographique exhaustive afin de situer au mieux le sujet et sa complexité. Développer des architectures de transistors à électron unique (SET) dans une technologie CMOS FDSOI avancée. Implémenter une architecture de qubit innovante (passage d’une structure linéaire 1D à une matrice 2D). Optimiser le layout des qubits en tirant parti des techniques de lithographie avancées utilisées dans les technologies FDSOI. Effectuer des simulations 3D, embarquer des structures de test et réaliser les dispositifs correspondants sur silicium. Caractériser les qubits et les SET en régime cryogénique Mener une caractérisation avancée des pièges dans les diélectriques à température ambiante et à basse température. A propos de vous Niveau Bac+5 (Master 2 ou diplôme d’ingénieur) en micro/nanoélectronique, physique des dispositifs, électronique ou physique quantique appliquée (ou formation équivalente). Bases solides en physique des semi-conducteurs, dispositifs MOSFET (FDSOI/FinFET) et compréhension d’une filière technologique CMOS. Expérience pratique en salle blanche, caractérisation électrique ou design de circuits/dispositifs appréciée. Bonnes capacités scientifiques (esprit critique, lecture d’articles) et compétences en programmation/outils numériques. Excellentes aptitudes en communication, anglais scientifique et travail en équipe interdisciplinaire. Les résultats attendus de cette recherche sont la conception, le développement et la compréhension des performances des nouvelles architectures des qubits et de SET intégrant des matériaux avancés, capables de satisfaire les exigences du calcul quantique. Contact: carlos-augusto.suarezsegovia@st.com ST est fière d’être certifiée parmi les 17 entreprises mondiales « Global Top Employers 2025 » et d’être la première et unique entreprise de semi-conducteurs à recevoir cette distinction. ST a été distinguée dans ce classement grâce à sa démarche d’amélioration continue, se démarquant notamment par son engagement en matière d’éthique et d’intégrité, de sens et de valeurs, d’organisation et de gestion du changement, ainsi que par sa stratégie commerciale et ses performances. En France, ST a également obtenu la labélisation Happy Trainee 2025. Nous cultivons un environnement de travail inclusif et diversifié, où la discrimination n’a pas sa place. Notre ambition est de recruter et de fidéliser des talents reflétant la richesse des sociétés dans lesquelles nous évoluons. Nous nous engageons à l’équité dans le développement des carrières, les opportunités professionnelles et la rémunération. Chez ST, nous encourageons les candidats qui ne remplissent pas forcément tous les critères à postuler, car nous croyons en la richesse des parcours variés et offrons de réelles opportunités d’apprentissage et d’évolution. Am Fraunhofer-Institut für Produktionstechnologie IPT in Aachen gestalten wir mit mehr als 450 Mitarbeitenden die Produktion der Zukunft - digital, nachhaltig und resilient. Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten Möglichkeit zur Promotion an der RWTH Aachen in einem selbst entwickelten Forschungsthema Ein exzellentes Netzwerk aus Wissenschaft und Industrie mit hervorragenden Karriereperspektiven Attraktive Zusatzleistungen wie Deutschlandticket-Zuschuss, Mitarbeitendenrabatte und attraktive Benefits Warum Fraunhofer IPT? Bei uns verbindest du wissenschaftliche Exzellenz mit praxisnaher Forschung. Du entwickelst Technologien, die unmittelbar in industriellen Anwendungen zum Einsatz kommen, übernimmst früh Verantwortung in Industrie- und Forschungsprojekten und schaffst gleichzeitig die Grundlage für deine wissenschaftliche Karriere - bis hin zur Promotion. Die nachhaltige Erhöhung des Anteils von Frauen in der Wissenschaft ist unser erklärtes Ziel. Mit unserem Karriereprogramm »Fraunhofer TALENTA« bieten wir Berufseinsteigerinnen und Young Professionals zusätzliche Qualifizierungs- und Vernetzungsangebote sowie den nötigen Freiraum zur Gestaltung ihres Karrierewegs. linkedin:4479827428.title: CRUK Black Leaders in Cancer PhD Scholarship
linkedin:4479827428.desc: 🎓 PhD Opportunity | Artificial Intelligence in Childhood Leukaemia Research 🔬 Interested in using AI and data science to advance childhood cancer research? The Leukaemia Research Cytogenomics Group (LRCG) at Newcastle University is recruiting a PhD student through the Cancer Research UK (CRUK) Black Leaders in Cancer PhD Scholarship Programme, with applications now open for the 2027 intake. This exciting project will focus on developing and evaluating trustworthy synthetic healthcare data using statistical methods, machine learning and generative AI, drawing on a national dataset of more than 20,000 childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) patients. The research aims to support more robust, reproducible and privacy-conscious approaches to childhood leukaemia research, with the potential to improve our understanding of treatment pathways and patient outcomes. 🔬 Project focus: Developing and comparing statistical, machine-learning and generative AI approaches to synthetic healthcare data generation. Evaluating the preservation of clinically important patterns, treatment pathways and outcomes, including rare events such as relapse. Assessing data utility, privacy, fidelity, fairness and clinical validity. Exploring the use of synthetic data for methodological research, hypothesis generation and reproducible analysis. 🌍 What the scholarship offers: Fully funded 4-year PhD, including stipend and tuition fees (Home fee status). Mentoring and leadership development opportunities. Networking through Black in Cancer and the Windsor Fellowship. A supportive and diverse research environment. Opportunities for research placements and community engagement. 👩‍💻 Who should apply? We welcome applicants with backgrounds in statistics, data science, biostatistics, epidemiology, computer science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related quantitative disciplines. As part of the CRUK Black Leaders in Cancer Programme, we particularly encourage applications from talented Black students who are passionate about advancing cancer research and addressing inequalities in healthcare. 📍 Location: Newcastle University, UK 👨‍🏫 Primary Supervisor: Dr. Amir Enshaei 📅 Application deadline: 4 December 2026 🎓 Start: 2027 intake 🔗 Find out more and apply: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/cancer/training/studentships/cruk-black-leaders-phd/ For informal enquiries, please contact Amir Enshaei (Primary Supervisor). Join us in advancing AI-driven research to improve outcomes for children with leukaemia! #PhDOpportunity #PhDStudentship #BlackLeadersInCancer #CancerResearch #ArtificialIntelligence #MachineLearning #DataScience #ChildhoodLeukaemia #SyntheticData #NewcastleUniversity

linkedin:4479714389.title: Doktorandplats - statistiker inom tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården
linkedin:4479714389.desc: Vid Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS) bedrivs världsledande forskning inom åldrande, demens, epidemiologi och vårdvetenskap. Forskningen sträcker sig från grundforskning på molekyl- och cellnivå till kliniska studier och forskning på samhällsnivå. Vid NVS genomför cirka en tredjedel av KI:s studenter sin utbildning på grund- och avancerad nivå. Institutionen med cirka 540 anställda och en omsättning på 530 miljoner miljoner år 2023, består av sju avdelningar och finns på Campus Flemingsberg och Campus Solna. Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård ansvarar för delar av läkarprogrammet. Inom forskarutbildning har vi en egen forskarskola i allmänmedicin. Vår primärvårdsforskning omfattar varierande projekt kring multisjuklighet, folksjukdomar som diabetes, nedsatt njurfunktion och psykisk ohälsa samt även pedagogiska projekt. Närmare 100 personer, av vilka cirka 30 doktorander, är anknutna till avdelningen. Vill du bidra till medicinsk forskning av toppkvalitet? Att vara doktorand innebär att vara antagen till en utbildning på forskarnivå (forskarutbildning) där man följer en individuell studieplan. En doktorand ägnar sig åt ett forskningsprojekt under handledning, kompletterat med kurser och andra lärandeaktiviteter. För en doktorsexamen krävs motsvarande fyra års utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid. Forskargruppen Doktorandtjänsten finns inom forskargruppen för STEADY-CAN (Stockholm Early Detection of Cancer Study) vid Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård, Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS). Gruppen består av kliniskt aktiva forskare, statistiker och doktorander som arbetar med tidig upptäckt av cancer, i nära samarbete med Regionalt cancercentrum Stockholm-Gotland och internationella samarbetspartners. Gruppen är involverad i flera pågående forskningsprojekt, inklusive utveckling av statistiska och maskininlärningsbaserade prediktionsmodeller, longitudinell analys av blodprovsdata och registerbaserade kohortstudier inom cancerepidemiologi. Du kommer att ingå i en tvärvetenskaplig grupp där statistiker, allmänläkare och epidemiologer arbetar nära varandra. I praktiken innebär det att du regelbundet diskuterar analysval med kliniker, förklarar statistiska metoder för personer utan statistisk bakgrund och själv lär dig om den kliniska vardagen i primärvården. Gruppen har regelbundna gemensamma analysmöten där du förväntas både ge och ta emot återkoppling på pågående arbete. Doktorandprojektet och doktorandens uppgifter Detta doktorandprojekt kombinerar traditionell statistisk modellering och maskininlärning i tillämpad forskning kring tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården. Projektet använder data från STEADY-CAN-kohorten, som omfattar över 2,7 miljoner vuxna i Region Stockholm med länkade laboratorie-, journal- och registerdata. Under doktorandutbildningen kommer kandidaten att få bred kunskap inom överlevnadsanalys, prediktionsmodellering, maskininlärning och hantering av stora registerbaserade datamängder. Vi söker en motiverad doktorand med god bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. Den framgångsrika kandidaten förväntas ta ett stort eget ansvar genom hela projektet, med stöd från handledarna. Detta innebär konstruktion av analysdatamängder, statistisk analys och implementering av maskininlärningsmetoder, författande av vetenskapliga artiklar samt deltagande i institutionens seminarier och i nationella och internationella konferenser. Vad erbjuder vi? En kreativ, internationell och inspirerande miljö fylld av kompetens och nyfikenhet. Karolinska Institutet är ett av världens ledande medicinska universitet. Här bedriver vi framgångsrik medicinsk forskning och har det största utbudet av medicinska utbildningar i Sverige. På KI får du träffa forskare med olika forskningsinriktningar som jobbar tillsammans. Det är det gränsöverskridande samarbetet som bidrar till KI:s världsledande position inom forskning. Som doktorand erbjuds du ett individuellt forskningsprojekt, en välutbildad handledare, ett stort utbud av valbara kurser och möjligheten att arbeta i en framgångsrik forskargrupp. Karolinska Institutet har samarbeten med framstående universitet över hela världen, vilket ger möjlighet till internationella utbyten. Som anställd doktorand får du en avtalsenlig lön, du får träna fritt i våra moderna friskvårdsanläggningar och du får ersättning för läkarvård. Behörighetskrav för utbildning på forskarnivå För att delta i urvalet till en doktorandplats måste du styrka både det grundläggande (A) och det särskilda (B) behörighetskravet innan ansökningsperioden stänger. Det är ditt ansvar som sökande att styrka din behörighet genom att följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. A) Grundläggande behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det grundläggande behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: har avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå (magister- eller masterexamen), eller har fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller har på annat sätt förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.* Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. *Om du anser dig ha motsvarande kunskaper ska du följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Bedömning av motsvarande kunskaper för grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. B) Särskilt behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det särskilda behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: - Intygar kunskaper i engelska (motsvarande Engelska B/Engelska 6 vid gymnasiet med godkänt betyg). Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan English language requirements for doctoral education. Kontroll av dokument Karolinska Institutet gör kontroll av dokumenten för att upptäcka förfalskningar. Karolinska Institutet förbehåller sig rätten att återkalla antagningsbeslut om förfalskningar eller oriktigheter påvisas. Inlämnande av falska handlingar är ett brott mot svensk lag och anses vara grund för rättsliga åtgärder. Färdigheter och personliga egenskaper Den sökande bör ha en gedigen bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. En examen i statistik/biostatistik eller matematisk statistik på avancerad nivå, t.ex. en masterexamen, är starkt meriterande. Utmärkta kunskaper i biostatistik och praktisk erfarenhet av överlevnadsanalys är meriterande. Tidigare erfarenhet av databehandling och statistisk analys är meriterande. Dessa erfarenheter ska företrädesvis vara från en medicinsk forskningsmiljö. Mycket goda kunskaper i statistisk programmering, företrädesvis i R, är avgörande för rollen. Erfarenhet av arbete med svenska registerdata är meriterande. Ett starkt intresse för medicinsk forskning i kombination med en passion för att tillämpa statistiska metoder för att besvara kliniskt relevanta forskningsfrågor är mycket önskvärt. Då STEADY-CAN-databasen, inklusive journal- och registervariabler och tillhörande beskrivningar, är på svenska är goda kunskaper i svenska i tal och skrift ett krav. Handledningen och det internationella samarbetet sker delvis på engelska, varför goda kunskaper även i engelska i tal och skrift också krävs. Den sökande ska ha god kommunikationsförmåga, vilket är avgörande för att samarbeta med tvärvetenskapliga team och effektivt presentera forskningsresultat. Vi lägger mycket stor vikt vid personliga egenskaper i denna rekrytering. Den idealiska kandidaten bör vara: Självständig, strukturerad och med stark analytisk förmåga. Flexibel och ivrig att lära. Denna roll innebär kontinuerligt lärande och anpassning till nya metoder och utmaningar. Öppen för konstruktiva synpunkter och förmåga att delta i balanserad, analytisk självreflektion. Kandidaten ska även trivas med att arbeta i team och samarbeta väl med teammedlemmar med olika akademisk bakgrund. Förklara i ditt personliga brev hur du uppfyller de nödvändiga färdigheterna och egenskaperna. Villkor Doktorandplatsen innebär en anställning som doktorand under maximalt 4 år på heltid. Ansökan Du söker doktorandplatsen i rekryteringsverktyget Varbi. Använd knappen uppe till höger och följ anvisningarna. Vi ser gärna att din ansökan är skriven på engelska, men det går också bra att ansöka på svenska. Din ansökan ska innehålla dessa dokument: - Ett personligt brev och curriculum vitae - Eventuella examensarbeten och publikationer - Andra dokument som styrker de ovan efterfrågade färdigheter och egenskaper - Dokument som styrker det grundläggande behörighetskravet (se A ovan) - Dokument som styrker det särskilda behörighetskravet (se B ovan) Urval Urval bland behöriga sökande görs med hänsyn till deras förmåga att tillgodogöra sig forskarutbildning. En samlad bedömning av de sökandes meriter och lämplighet kommer att göras. Följande bedömningsgrunder tillämpas vid Karolinska Institutet: - Dokumenterade ämneskunskaper av betydelse för forskningsområdet - Analytisk skicklighet - Övriga dokumenterade kunskaper/erfarenheter som kan ha betydelse för aktuell forskarutbildning Alla sökanden kommer att få information när rekryteringen är slutförd. KI tillämpar en lönestege vid lönesättning av doktorander. NVS Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård Vill du göra skillnad - och bidra till en bättre hälsa för alla? Sök till Karolinska Institutet Vid Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS) bedrivs världsledande forskning inom åldrande, demens, epidemiologi och vårdvetenskap. Forskningen sträcker sig från grundforskning på molekyl- och cellnivå till kliniska studier och forskning på samhällsnivå. Vid NVS genomför cirka en tredjedel av KI:s studenter sin utbildning på grund- och avancerad nivå. Institutionen med cirka 540 anställda och en omsättning på 530 miljoner miljoner år 2023, består av sju avdelningar och finns på Campus Flemingsberg och Campus Solna.

linkedin:4479154787.title: Phd candidate - Generative Agent-Based Modeling for Climate Policy Design
linkedin:4479154787.desc: Tecnun - Escuela de Ingeniería-Universidad de Navarra Tecnun-Escuela de Ingeniería , perteneciente a la Universidad de Navarra , se propone contribuir a la formación profesional, científica y humana de los futuros ingenieros. Desde su creación, en la primavera de 1961, mantiene un equilibrio entre la docencia, la investigación y el servicio a la sociedad, haciendo que estas actividades se complementen entre sí. Actualmente dispone de dos campus : la sede más antigua, ubicada en el campus universitario del Bº de Ibaeta, está integrada por los edificios de laboratorios, el edificio docente y de representación concluido en 1989, y un edificio multiuso, levantado en 1996. La otra sede se encuentra en el Parque Tecnológico de Miramón e integra las aulas y laboratorios de investigación de las áreas de Electricidad, Electrónica y Comunicaciones. Descripción de la oferta Fully Funded PhD Opportunity at TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra, Spain We are seeking a highly motivated PhD Researcher to join our team for a 3- to 4-year fully funded PhD opportunity. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, and Policy Modelling to build advanced decision-support tools for climate action and disaster resilience. The candidate will be part of the Resilience research group at TECNUN, which focuses on understanding and strengthening the resilience of communities, cities, and organizations in the face of disruptions and crises. The group combines engineering, data-driven approaches, and decision-support methodologies, with research spanning areas such as urban resilience, crisis management, infrastructure, and emerging technologies such as AI and LLMs. The PhD candidate will join this research environment under the supervision of Professor Josune Hernantes and Dr. Sahar Elkady. About The Project This PhD project focuses on developing a novel decision-support framework that combines Generative Agent-Based Modelling (GABM) with Simulation Optimization. The primary goal is to simulate how diverse societal stakeholders (e.g., citizens, businesses, and public authorities) interact, perceive, and respond to climate-related policies. By integrating LLM-driven generative agents into an optimization loop, the project aims to help decision-makers design robust policies that balance environmental targets with public acceptance and social legitimacy. Main Duties And Responsibilities The PhD candidate will conduct research leading to the development of their doctoral thesis, with the aim of disseminating their findings through high-quality publications in highly ranked, internationally recognized journals. The candidate will be expected to take an active role in the development and execution of research projects related to their research topic, as well as contribute to the preparation and submission of research proposals and funding applications. The candidate should also be willing to actively participate in seminars, workshops, meetings, and other activities organized by the Department and the research group. As part of the responsibilities established in the PhD student agreement, the candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching activities, including serving as a teaching assistant in selected courses and proctoring examinations. These responsibilities are intended to provide the candidate with broader academic and professional development alongside their research activities. Requisitos Provisions relating to positions as PhD Research Fellows can be found in the Applied Engineering program web page. Education: MSc degree in Computer Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computational Social Science, or a closely related field. Technical Skills: Solid background in computational modelling, simulation, or optimization techniques. Programming proficiency in Python (experience with LLM frameworks, prompt engineering, or agent-based frameworks is a strong plus). Familiarity with machine learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), or natural language processing. Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities, excellent writing skills for scientific publications, and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary team. We recognize that candidates may have different academic and professional backgrounds. If you do not meet all of the requirements but believe that your skills, experience, and motivation make you a strong potential candidate, we still encourage you to apply. We look forward to hearing from you. Application Applicants Should Submit a Dossier Including: Detailed Curriculum Vitae including all the relevant projects/publications. Certificates and transcripts of the bachelor's and master's degrees. Applicants with foreign higher education must attach an official description of the grading system used at the issuing institution. One-page summary of MSc’s thesis The names and contact details of two references. A one-page document answering the following questions (Please describe any relevant academic, research, or practical experience, including optimization, mathematical modelling, simulation, or related methods): What is your experience with ABM? What is your experience with LLM and Software Engineering? What is your experience with Operations Research? For further information or queries, please contact Sahar Elkady at selkady@unav.es. About The University The University of Navarra is an international University committed to quality teaching and excellence in research. It occupies the 3rd position in the Europe Teaching Ranking 2019 by Times Higher Education and Elsevier. The University was founded on the basis of Catholic principles by St. Josemaría Escrivá and is a corporate work of Opus Dei. It supports the professional development of its faculty and staff, promotes cultural engagement and social outreach through collaboration with NGOs and charitable organizations, and encourages service-learning initiatives. Employment opportunities are offered fairly, with all qualified candidates considered equally. The School of Engineering (TECNUN) is home to approximately 1,200 students and is located in Donostia-San Sebastián, a vibrant and picturesque city on Spain’s northern Basque coast. As an academic institution, TECNUN conducts fundamental research across a broad range of engineering disciplines while also fostering strong links between academic research and real-world applications. In this context, TECNUN collaborates closely with CEIT, a non-profit applied research Centre founded by the University of Navarra in 1982. This partnership facilitates the transfer of scientific knowledge into innovative technological solutions and strengthens the connection between fundamental research, applied research, and industrial needs. For further information about the School of Engineering, the University of Navarra, and the city of Donostia-San Sebastián, please visit the following websites: University of Navarra (UNAV), TECNUN – School of Engineering, and Donostia-San Sebastián. indeed:b4d5926c58f63991.title: PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI
indeed:b4d5926c58f63991.desc: The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI. The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions. Project description The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment. The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team. Description of the scientific environment The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ . This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk ) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk ) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam Who are we looking for? Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems. The PhD programme You can undertake the PhD programme as: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree. Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme Qualifications needed for the regular programme To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria: You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; You must work on the project full-time. Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality. Terms of employment in the regular programme Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years. Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant. Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure. Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network Disseminate research nationally and internationally Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project We are looking for the following qualifications: Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position Relevant educational background Relevant publications Relevant work experience Other relevant professional activities Good written and oral English language skills Application and Assessment Procedure Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. Please include : Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications ; Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; Publication list (if available); Names and contact details of three references. Application deadline: The deadline for applications is November 22 , 23:59 GMT +1 . We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements. The further process After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment. The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/. Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in December Questions For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact ias@di.ku.dk General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/. The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position. Vi sikrer traditionsrige og moderne rammer om uddannelser og fri forskning på højt internationalt niveau. Vi søger svar og løsninger på fælles problemer og gør ny viden tilgængelig og nyttig for andre. indeed:70994ae299f9146b.title: Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology at the University of Oulu (Finland)
indeed:70994ae299f9146b.desc: The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles. We are currently looking for a Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology to join research projects focusing on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), teacher education, and teachers’ professional development at the Faculty of Education and Psychology at the University of Oulu, Finland. The position is connected to two research projects: INTEGRATE – Training Teachers to Integrate EU Matters through GenAI-Supported Pedagogy and The Power of Teachers' Online Mentorship for AI Partnership (Power T/A) . The INTEGRATE project, funded by the Erasmus+ Programme under the Jean Monnet Teacher Training action, aims to empower pre-service and in-service teachers to integrate EU topics and values into everyday teaching through GenAI-supported pedagogy. The project develops and implements teacher education courses, online professional development modules, instructional materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities. The Power T/A project, funded by the Research Council of Finland, explores the integration of AI-based technologies into teacher mentorship and instructional activities. The project focuses on how AI technologies can support teachers’ professional development, particularly through online mentorship, and how teachers can develop the knowledge and skills needed for meaningful AI integration in education. About the job As a doctoral researcher, you will: Conduct doctoral research within the INTEGRATE (75%) and Power T/A (25%) projects, with a focus on GenAI, teacher education, and teachers’ professional learning. Contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of GenAI-supported teacher education and professional development activities . Participate in the development and implementation of courses, online professional development modules, case-based learning materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities for teachers. Collect and analyse qualitative and quantitative research data related to the implementation and evaluation of project activities. Contribute to scientific publications and other research outputs arising from the projects. Collaborate with teachers, teacher educators, researchers, and national and international project partners. Present research findings at scientific conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results. In this role, you will become part of a dynamic and supportive research environment focusing on educational technology, teacher education, and the pedagogically meaningful and responsible use of artificial intelligence. Qualifications To succeed in the position, we expect from you: A Master’s degree in education, educational technology, educational psychology, or another relevant discipline. A strong interest in research on Generative AI, educational technology, teacher education, and EU matters and values. Proficiency in qualitative and/or quantitative research methods and the ability to apply these methods in educational research. Good IT and data analysis skills and an interest in using digital and AI-based tools in educational research. Fluent written and spoken English. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary and international research environments. Additional merits considered an advantage Familiarity with the Finnish K–12 education system and/or teacher education . Experience working with pre-service or in-service teachers . Experience in teaching, teacher education, professional development, or instructional design . Experience or demonstrated interest in AI/GenAI-supported teaching and learning . Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research data collection and analysis. Familiarity with technology-enhanced learning environments. Finnish language skills (not required but considered as an advantage). What we offer? indeed:571be3fb97a6761d.title: Doctorat (H/F) en Web Sémantique et Intelligence Artificielle
indeed:571be3fb97a6761d.desc: L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Laboratoire d'Informatique, Signaux et Systèmes de Sophia Antipolis Type de Contrat CDD Doctorant Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 06903 VALBONNE Durée du contrat 36 mois Date d'Embauche 01/01/2027 Rémuneration 2300,00 € mensuel Date limite de candidature : vendredi 6 novembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Sujet De Thèse Dans le cadre du projet ANR DIVA, cette thèse se concentrera sur la modélisation sémantique et la représentation en graphes de connaissances de l’activité analytique des utilisateurs, ainsi que sur l’étude d’approches neuro-symboliques pour apprendre et raisonner sur ces représentations. L’objectif est ainsi de poser les fondations nécessaires à la prédiction de comportements et, à terme, au développement de mécanismes de recommandation et d’adaptation des visualisations explicables et contrôlables. Malgré des travaux importants sur la capture et la visualisation des traces d'activité des utilisateurs, les représentations existantes sont généralement propriétaires ou ad hoc [1], ce qui limite le raisonnement automatisé, l'interopérabilité et la réutilisation à long terme. Les graphes de connaissances (GC), fondés sur les normes du Web sémantique telles que RDF, RDFS et OWL, offrent une alternative prometteuse pour représenter l'activité des utilisateurs sous forme de données liées et riches sur le plan sémantique [3]. Ils permettent notamment de structurer et intégrer des données d'activité hétérogènes, tout en fournissant des mécanismes standardisés d'interrogation et de raisonnement. Cette représentation constitue ainsi un support pertinent pour l'application de méthodes d'IA visant à identifier des comportements analytiques et à en prédire l'évolution, tout en conservant une représentation explicite et interprétable des connaissances. S'appuyant sur des travaux antérieurs (par exemple, UI2Ont [4] et DIVA [5], et des ensembles de données ouverts sur l'activité des utilisateurs [6], cette thèse de doctorat vise à développer des modèles sémantiques et des approches neuro-symboliques pour la représentation et l'analyse de l'activité utilisateur. Elle s'articule autour des objectifs suivants : Modélisation sémantique de l'activité de l'utilisateur : Développer un cadre unifié, fondé sur des vocabulaires RDF, pour représenter l'activité multimodale de l'utilisateur sous forme de GC, en intégrant et structurant les données hétérogènes générées lors de l'exploration visuelle, notamment les interactions de l'utilisateur, le suivi du regard et les verbalisations. Découverte et prédiction du comportement exploratoire de l'utilisateur : Étudier des méthodes neuro-symboliques permettant d'exploiter les GC pour découvrir et prédire des comportements exploratoires, en combinant apprentissage automatique et raisonnement symbolique afin d'identifier des modèles comportementaux interprétables. Raffinement dynamique et validation des modèles comportamentaux : Étudier des méthodes de raffinement incrémental des modèles et règles comportementaux au cours de l'exploration, et évaluer leur qualité, leur interprétabilité et leurs capacités prédictives dans différents scénarios d'utilisation. Plan de travail : La thèse débutera par une revue de l’état de l’art, suivie du développement et de la validation du modèle sémantique et des pipelines de construction des graphes de connaissances. Les travaux porteront ensuite sur la découverte et la prédiction des comportements exploratoires à l’aide de méthodes neuro-symboliques, puis sur leur raffinement dynamique et incrémental. Les approches développées seront évaluées sur des données réelles et donneront lieu à des publications scientifiques ainsi qu’à des contributions open source. Les livrables attendus sont : L1. Modèle sémantique et extension de DIVA-O pour l’activité utilisateur multimodale. L2. Pipeline de construction et d’enrichissement des graphes de connaissances. L3. Méthodes neuro-symboliques pour la découverte et la prédiction des comportements exploratoires. L4. Méthodes de raffinement dynamique des modèles comportementaux. L5. Évaluation expérimentale des modèles et méthodes proposés. L6. Publications scientifiques et ressources open source. Références Bibliographiques [3] H. Paulheim and F. Probst, “A Formal Ontology on User Interfaces – Yet Another User Interface Description Language?,” 2011. [4] H. Paulheim and F. Probst, “UI2Ont—A Formal Ontology on User Interfaces and Interactions,” in Semantic Models for Adaptive Interactive Systems, T. Hussein, H. Paulheim, S. Lukosch, J. Ziegler, and G. Calvary, Eds., London: Springer, 2013, pp. 1–24. doi: 10.1007/978-1-4471-5301-6_1. [5] A. Menin and C. Faron, “DIVA: An Ontology-based Approach to Model User Activity within Visualization Systems,” in SAC 2026 - 41st ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing, Thessaloniki, Greece, Mar. 2026. doi: 10.1145/3748522.3779893. [6] S. Mohseni, A. Pachuilo, E. H. Nirjhar, R. Linder, A. Pena, and E. D. Ragan, “Analytic Provenance Datasets: A Data Repository of Human Analysis Activity and Interaction Logs,” Jan. 16, 2018, arXiv: arXiv:1801.05076. doi: 10.48550/arXiv.1801.05076. Votre Environnement de Travail Cette thèse est accueillie par le laboratoire I3S du CNRS à l’Université Côte d’Azur. Plus précisément, le/la doctorant(e) rejoindra l’équipe Wimmics (Inria, Université Côte d’Azur, CNRS, I3S), qui mène des recherches à l’interface entre intelligence artificielle et Web, notamment autour des graphes de connaissances, de la représentation et du traitement sémantique des données, et des méthodes d’IA pour les données du Web. Cette thèse s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet ANR JCJC DIVA, qui vise à étudier comment l’activité des utilisateurs avec des systèmes de visualisation interactifs peut être capturée, représentée et exploitée afin de mieux comprendre et, à terme, accompagner leurs processus d’analyse. Le projet part du constat que les interactions des utilisateurs avec les visualisations constituent une source riche d’information sur leurs processus analytiques, leurs stratégies et leurs objectifs, mais que les approches existantes reposent souvent sur des représentations ad hoc, limitant leur interopérabilité, leur réutilisation et le raisonnement automatisé [1], [2]. DIVA vise ainsi à développer des approches sémantiques et neuro-symboliques pour représenter l’activité des utilisateurs et identifier des comportements analytiques à partir de leurs traces d’interaction avec le système, des données biometriques, ainsi que des verbalisations sur leur raisonnement. Références [1] K. Xu, A. Ottley, C. Walchshofer, M. Streit, R. Chang, and J. Wenskovitch, “Survey on the Analysis of User Interactions and Visualization Provenance,” Comput. Graph. Forum, vol. 39, no. 3, pp. 757–783, 2020. [2] F. Yanez, C. Conati, A. Ottley, and C. Nobre, “The State of the Art in User‐Adaptive Visualizations,” Comput. Graph. Forum, vol. 44, Dec. 2024, doi: 10.1111/cgf.15271. indeed:9ba5ddf6aae2fa47.title: PhD Position - Translational Neuroscience
indeed:9ba5ddf6aae2fa47.desc: PhD Position - Translational Neuroscience We are looking for a PhD candidate to join the Multimodal Imaging in Clinical Neuroscience department at the Institute of Neuroscience and Medicine – Medical Imaging Physics (INM-4). You will work in the field of translational neuroscience and precision psychiatry under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Irene Neuner and Dr. Ravichandran Rajkumar. The brain mechanisms underlying psychiatric disorders are poorly understood, and treatment choices are largely symptom-based. In this project, you will use multimodal neuroimaging and computational neuroscience to study how brain networks change in these disorders. The aim is to identify imaging biomarkers that could support earlier diagnosis, predict disease trajectories at an individual level and help match treatment to the patient. A key resource is our MINDset platform (Multimodal Imaging Infrastructure for Neuroscience Data Science), which consolidates over 1,000 multimodal datasets from clinical studies, including structural and functional MRI, PET, EEG, fNIRS, neuropsychological and clinical measures, and digital phenotyping. Vertragsart: Vollzeit Angebot Team & Environment: You will work in a motivated and interdisciplinary team including psychiatrists, neuroscientists, physicists, engineers, and data scientists Research & Infrastructure: You will have access to advanced neuroimaging infrastructure and training in structural and functional MRI, multimodal imaging, connectomics, and computational neuroscience Networking & Exchange: You will participate in (international) conferences and project meetings, actively building your scientific network through collaborations involving Forschungszentrum Jülich, RWTH Aachen University, Ulm University, Bezirkskrankenhaus Günzburg and LVR-Klinik Cologne Supervision & Support: We will accompany your doctoral studies with continuous, expert guidance from your academic supervisors Prof. Dr. Irene Neuner and Dr. Ravichandran Rajkumar Work-life balance: Optimal conditions for balancing work and private life, as well as a family-friendly company policy. The option of flexible working (in terms of location) is generally available after consultation and in line with upcoming tasks and (on-site) appointments Annual Leave: You get 30 days of annual leave Fixed-term: The position is limited to 3 years Fair remuneration: Depending on your existing qualifications and the tasks assigned to you, you will be classified in pay grade 13 (65 %) of the TVöD-Bund (Collective Agreement for the Public Service). In addition to the basic salary, there is an additional year-end bonus under the collective pay agreement amounting to 75% of a monthly salary, as well as capital-forming benefits. All information on the TVöD-Bund collective agreement can be found on the BMI website. The monthly salaries in euros can be found on page 74 of the PDF download Support for international employees: Our International Advisory Service makes it easier for international employees to get started In addition to exciting tasks and a collegial working environment, we offer you much more: https://go.fzj.de/benefits Aufgaben The successful candidate will have the opportunity to combine prospectively acquired data with existing multimodal datasets and contribute to replication studies, biomarker development, machine learning applications, and analyses of individual disease trajectories. Your tasks will include: Integrate multimodal neuroimaging datasets from MRI, PET, EEG, and fNIRS studies Characterize brain networks using graph-theoretical methods and structural and functional connectivity analyses Apply multivariate statistical modelling and machine learning to multimodal datasets Investigate individualized imaging biomarkers relevant to diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring Coordinate longitudinal studies involving psychiatric patients and healthy controls, including recruitment, scheduling, and neuropsychological and psychopathological assessments Coordinate and supervise MRI data acquisition; maintain standardized acquisition protocols and data quality Manage and curate imaging data in accordance with established standards (e.g., BIDS) Profil Excellent university degree (Master) in neuroscience, biomedical engineering, medical physics, psychology, cognitive science, computer science, physics, data science, or a related discipline A strong interest in translational psychiatry, neuroimaging and computational neuroscience, and a motivation to work in an interdisciplinary research environment Programming experience in MATLAB and/or Python, alongside strong analytical and problem-solving skills Experience with structural and/or functional MRI; familiarity with packages such as SPM, FSL, FreeSurfer, AFNI, MRtrix, CONN, or similar tools is desirable Knowledge of neuroimaging preprocessing, quality control, graph theory, connectomics, multivariate statistics, or machine learning is an advantage Very good command of written and spoken English with extensive vocabulary is required (at least B2 level according to the CEFR), ideally supported by a certificate confirming the language level German language skills at B1 level are desirable Über uns We welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds, e.g. in terms of age, gender, disability, sexual orientation / identity, and social, ethnic and religious origin. A diverse and inclusive working environment with equal opportunities in which everyone can realize their potential is important to us. indeed:ff65bf913a18e175.title: PhD in Data- and AI-based solutions to improve child health and outcomes through housing
indeed:ff65bf913a18e175.desc: Sustainability, in its broadest definition, is the cornerstone of research and education in the Department of Built Environment. We take the lead in (re)shaping the built environment to be future-proof, safe, healthy, inclusive and respectful of planetary boundaries. We house the entire spectrum of technology, engineering, design, and human behavior disciplines in the built environment, with world-class experimental facilities at all scales. This allows us to address societal challenges from a uniquely integrated perspective. Introduction Are you a graduate in exact sciences, engineering or econometrics, passionate about using data and AI to improve people's lives?Eindhoven University of Technology is looking for a PhD candidate to develop innovative data-driven solutions that predict and optimise the impact of housing improvements on children's health and wellbeing. Job Description Millions of children, even in high-income countries, are born and grow up in homes with poor insulation, inadequate heating, or insufficient ventilation, affecting their health and development. While housing upgrades are often motivated by sustainability and affordability goals, we focus on their potential benefits for future generations. How does inadequate housing during pregnancy and early childhood affect children's health and development? Which housing upgrades offer the greatest benefits? And how can behavioural modelling, big data and AI help shape healthier, more equitable homes? These are the questions your PhD research will tackle. You will join an interdisciplinary team of researchers and practitioners, working at the intersection of housing, public health, climate adaptation, and social equity. Combining medical and behavioural insights, large-scale data analysis, computer vision and advanced statistical methods, you will be tranforming complex unstructured housing and health data into predictive models. The results will feed into a digital tool to predict and optimise the impact of housing upgrades across different scenarios, helping housing providers and municipalities create healthier, more resilient homes for families. This research is part of the NWO-funded research programme Homes for Upcoming Generations, which brings together social scientists, medical doctors, building engineers and industry partners. As a PhD candidate, you will be part of the TU/e's internationally renowned Urban Systems and Real Estate group (Department of the Built Environment), conducting cutting-edge research at the intersection of urban systems, real estate, data science, and smart technologies. The four-year program combines advanced training with impactful research, offering strong support for professional development through courses, seminars, and international conferences. You will collaborate closely with scientific partners at Erasmus Medical Centre, Erasmus University Rotterdam, VU University Amsterdam, as well as societal partners including housing providers, municipalities and engineering bureaus. Job Requirements The candidates should have: An MSc degree in Exact or data sciences/ Quantitative economics/ Engineering. A strong educational track-record including at least several of the following subjects: calculus, linear algebra, computational modelling, microeconomics, econometrics, operations research, data science. A proven experience of programming in Python and working with (big) data. Having working experience at a European research institute or a European university is an advantage. Strong demonstrable analytical skills and proficiency in English (spoken and written). Affinity with collaboration with industry, ability to bring together fundamental and applied research. Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In addition, we offer you: Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. indeed:801909fe8646ceb5.title: PhD candidate 'Development of an integrated system for breast cancer imaging | focus point ultrasound'
indeed:801909fe8646ceb5.desc: Jouw functie Ultrasound and tomosynthesis are the most prevalent modalities used for breast imaging, and each has its specific advantages and disadvantages. Ultrasound uses sound waves to create a cross-sectional image of the tissue and has excellent depth resolution, but limited resolution in directions perpendicular to the transmitted ultrasound lines. Tomosynthesis uses x rays to create a pseudo-3D representation of the breast with high in-plane spatial resolution, but low out-of-plane (depth) resolution. Therefore, both techniques are complementary to each other. We plan to develop a joint system that will use the information from each modality to improve the image quality of the other, yielding not only a multi-modality imaging system, but a joint imaging system. The combination of tomosynthesis and ultrasound into a single joint imaging system will yield improved images from two independent and complementary sources, with inherent spatial correlation, allowing for improved lesion detection, even in dense breasts, and the direct multi-modal assessment of suspicious lesions. For this multi-disciplinary project, we will be working in collaboration with the Advanced X-ray Tomography Imaging (AXTI) lab of our Department, who will be developing the X-ray aspects of this system (see accompanying vacancy). In this project, you will focus on 3D ultrasound by using an ultra-wide ultrasound transducer that is mounted in a paddle required for acquisition of tomosynthesis data. In this way, a 3D ultrasound dataset can be acquired that can be used to improve the x-ray data by using the high-axial resolution US data. Additionally, the ultrasound data can be improved by using the high-resolution x-ray data. You will develop and validate these methods using both digital and physical phantoms, working towards first patient images at the end of the project. All of this will be in collaboration with a PhD student focusing on the x-ray aspects of the project, and industry partners to facilitate the translation of these methods into clinical evaluation. Tasks will also include presenting at international scientific conferences and writing papers on the newly developed methods and study results.
